title: French Government grants from the French Embassy in Gabon - Master and PhD
synthese: A system of co-financed scholarships called "Concorde scholarships" is set up for the benefit of selected Gabonese students, "Concorde scholarship holders". At the end of the selection, 90 scholarship holders will benefit from the status of scholarship holder from the French government and the Gabonese government durin
description: The "Concorde" scholarships were set up in 2011 and extended to expire by a partnership agreement between the French Embassy in Gabon and the Gabon National Bursary Agency (ANBG). The program aims to enable an annual contingent of 90 Gabonese students to pursue studies in France. Students selected under the program benefit from the dual status of scholarship holders from the French (BGF) and Gabonese governments. Students who have completed a first cycle of higher studies in Gabon for a period of two or three years and who wish to enroll in a master's or doctorate cycle in a large French public school or university are eligible. The cooperation and cultural action department of the French Embassy and the ANBG sit equally on a mixed committee for the preselection of files. The ANBG undertakes to submit the list of candidates selected by the pre-selection committee to the Technical Commission of the ANBG. The application procedures are announced each year by the ANBG in a press release and on its website www.anbg-ga.com
montant: The French Party undertakes to pay for Concorde scholarship holders: - free registration at the university or in a public higher education establishment in France, - free access to the "Welcome to France" training - costs relating to social cover, - For the 10 students accepted in the grandes écoles or in a specialized training course, the training costs the transport costs to the place of residence and the remaining part of the BGF study grant rate 2 beyond the allowance of the ANBG. Through Campus France, the Gabonese party (ANBG) ensures, for its part, the payment of the nominal amount of the Gabonese government scholarship in accordance with the texts in force in Gabon for the 90 scholarship holders, the outward journey- return to the place of residence for the remaining 80 scholarship holders.

title: Mitacs Globalink Research Award (GRA)
synthese: The Mitacs Globalink Research Award (GRA) supports research collaborations between Canada and select partner organizations and eligible countries and regions.
description: Under the joint supervision of a home and host professor, successful senior undergraduate students, graduate students, as well as postdoctoral fellows will receive a $6,000 research award to conduct a 12- to 24-week research project in the other country. Awards are offered in partnership with Mitacs's Canadian academic partners (and, in some cases, with Mitacs's international partners) and are subject to available funding. Mitacs Globalink Research Award (GRA) are currently available to researchers from over 70 universities in Canada. Since 2014, the French Embassy in Canada is associated with Mitacs to offer each year 15 mobility awards to Canadian students (outside Quebec) willing to have an experience in France.
montant: Students selected through a highly competitive process will receive a $6000 research award .
duree: Research project of 12 to 24 weeks in a foreign partner university.
age: Must be the legal age of majority in Canada ( 18 years of age or older )
conditions: Cannot undertake a research project at an institution where they have previously completed a degree Cannot hold more than one Globalink Research Award per academic lifetime Cannot have previously held a Mitacs-JSPS Summer Program award Must meet travel requirements for their intended destination, including visa and/or immigration requirements and associated documentation. Cannot undertake a research project in a country where they hold citizenship. However: Permanent residents or citizens of Canada who are enrolled in an eligible country other than Canada and who wish to do a project in Canada are eligible to apply Permanent residents or citizens of Canada who are enrolled in a Canadian institution and who hold citizenship in an eligible country may apply to do a project there Must be registered as full-time senior undergraduates, graduate students, or postdoctoral fellows at an eligible Canadian institution or eligible international institution and remain as such throughout their Globalink Research Award. Undergraduate applicants completing their first post-secondary degree must have completed their second year of studies prior to departure. All applicants enrolled in an undergraduate degree must have maintained a B average in their two most recent semesters prior to application. This average can be cumulative over the two semesters. Postdoctoral fellows may apply if their date of graduation from a PhD program is no more than five years prior to the proposed start date of the research project and they have postdoctoral status at an eligible institution.
inscription: Applications for the Globalink Research Award are open on an ongoing basis. However, applicants are advised to apply at least 16 weeks ahead of their planned start date. This is because it typically takes 10-12 weeks for Mitacs to communicate results to the applicants, followed by a few weeks to process the award, and for the applicants to complete their pre-departure preparations. Academic supervisors at Canadian institutions obtain endorsement from the Canadian institution before preparing the application. Please contact your local Mitacs Business Development representative for more information on what kind of endorsement is required for your project and to request an application package.
pieces: in addition to completing all the fields in the application form, applicants will be required to submit CVs, letters of support, and a research proposal.
selection: Additional information will be provided in the application package.
domainNote: Open to all fields.

title: AI4CI Scholarship – Avignon Université
synthese: The AI4CI Scholarship is intended for outstanding international students who have been admitted to the AI4CI Master's program at Avignon Université and have officially accepted their place in the program.
description: The European Master's program AI4CI trains experts in artificial intelligence for connected systems and Industry 4.0. Offered at 6 universities across Europe, it includes Erasmus+ mobility opportunities and company internships. The AI4CI Scholarship aims to promote access to the AI4CI Master's program offered by Avignon Université for deserving international students, in order to support their studies in Avignon leading to the completion of the AI4CI Master's degree.
montant: 4,000 euros per scholarship (paid in two installments) For the 2026/2027 academic year, 5 scholarships are offered for first-year Master's students (M1) and 3 scholarships for second-year Master's students (M2).
duree: 1 year
maitriseLangue: English level B2
conditions: This scholarship is subject to the publication of a call on the European Union platform (https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/calls-for-proposals).
inscription: Applications must be submitted online only via the dedicated European platform (information to be provided at a later date). The application submission period is set from June 21 to August 21, 2026.
pieces: Details will be available on the European application platform.
selection: A committee will review applications and select the recipients. Selected candidates will receive a confirmation letter. The committee's decision is final and not subject to appeal.
countryNote: Only students whose nationality appears on the list of eligible countries may apply for this scholarship
domainNote: Only students enrolled in the AI4CI program at Avignon Université are eligible
levelNote: Must demonstrate excellent academic achievement

title: Excellence Scholarship - emlyon business school
synthese: emlyon business school rewards outstanding candidates with Excellence Scholarship based on the applicant's profile.
description: At emlyon business school, we are committed to recognizing and rewarding exceptional talent. Our Excellence Scholarship is designed to support outstanding candidates who demonstrate academic excellence and leadership potential, as reflected in their application profile. We offer the following scholarship opportunities based on your performance in standardized management tests: 10% Scholarship: Awarded to students who achieve a GMAT score of 700 or above, a GMAT Focus score of 645 or above, an equivalent GRE score, or a Tage Mage score of 400 or more. 5% Scholarship: Awarded to students who achieve a GMAT score of 650 or above, a GMAT Focus score of 595 or above, an equivalent GRE score, or a Tage Mage score of 360 or more. We understand that the timing of your test results may not always align with your application process. Therefore, you have the flexibility to submit your management test scores even after you have completed your application and gained admission to the program. This ensures that you can still be considered for the Excellence Scholarship based on your most recent and best scores.

title: Individual Scholarship emlyon business school - Specialized programs (MSc/Master)
synthese: Scholarship of up to 50% according to individual criteria for students enrolled in MSc/Master programs.
description: Our programs MSc/Master offer individual scholarships designed to support high-potential and motivated candidates in achieving their academic goals, regardless of personal or financial circumstances. We believe that factors such as diversity, academic excellence, and financial need should be considered in building a dynamic and inclusive cohort. To apply for a scholarship, simply complete the individual scholarship request form and include it with your program application. This allows us to assess your eligibility and ensure that financial concerns do not hinder your pursuit of a world-class graduate education.

title: Excellence Scholarship Program - Social Coverage Scholarships (BCS)
synthese: This 3-year scholarship is a complement to the MENPS merit-based scholarship program. It enables selected students to obtain French government scholarship status and related benefits.
description: The Excellence Scholarship for French Grandes Ecoles is the result of a partnership between the Ministry of National Education, Preschool and Sports (MENPS) and the French Embassy in Morocco. Each year, the Franco-Moroccan selection committee awards 200 social coverage scholarships (BCS) to Moroccan students admitted to the 1st year of a Grande École of Engineering or Business in France. This 3-year scholarship, which is part of the MENPS merit-based scholarship program, enables the selected students to obtain French government scholarship status, as well as the associated benefits.
montant: 1. The BCS is awarded to students for the duration of their studies in France, 3 years. It is combined with the merit-based grant awarded by the MENPS. 2. The BCS entitles students to the status of “ French Government Scholarship Holder ”, with all the associated benefits: - Exemption from tuition fees at French institutions under the authority of the Ministry of Higher Education and Research (MESR - Ministère de l'Education, de la Recherche, de la Solidarité et de la Solidarité); - Exemption from differentiated fees for students from outside the European Union; - Coverage of health insurance; - Free visa fees; - Reimbursement of Campus France application fees; Registration.
conditions: - Be of Moroccan nationality - Be enrolled in the 2nd year of a CPGE in France or Morocco during the 2024-2025 academic year - Be admitted for the year, in respect of the 2025-2026 academic year, to a Grande École of Business or Engineering in France - Be a recipient of the merit scholarship from the Ministry of National Education, Preschool and Sports (MENPS)
inscription: Applications should be sent to www.ecpge.ac.ma at the same time as applications for the MENPS merit scholarship.

title: Marietta Blau Scholarship
synthese: The Marietta Blau scholarship from the Federal Ministry of Education, Science and Research (BMBWF) supports the completion of part (6-12 months) of a doctoral/PhD course abroad that was conducted in Austria.
description: The Marietta Blau scholarship from the Federal Ministry of Education, Science and Research (BMBWF) supports the completion of part (6-12 months) of a doctoral/PhD course abroad that was conducted in Austria. title: AlUla Scholarship Program
synthese: Campus France partner of the Royal Commission For AlUla, for the AlUla Scholarship Program
description: On April 10, 2018, France signed an agreement with Saudi Arabia to develop the archaeological site of AlUla, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and tourism in this region. The Campus France Agency has been appointed as the operator responsible for training future French-speaking Saudi experts from the AlUla region. As such, it implements an 8-year training course of approximately 200 to 500 Saudi students, scholarship holders of the Royal Commission For AlUla, divided into several annual cohorts. This training begins with the intensive learning of French in French as a Foreign Language centers for a period of one year and six months. Young Saudis who have obtained a B2 level are then selected to continue their training in France in Diploma, Licence or Master's degrees in fields such as Hospitality Management & Tourism, Agriculture, Archeology, Heritage and Urban Planning.

title: Erasmus+ grant
synthese: Under Erasmus+, students have the opportunity to spend part of their studies at a partner university in another European country or in a partner country worldwide.
description: Under Erasmus+, students have the opportunity to spend part of their studies at a partner university in another European country or in a partner country worldwide. The precondition is the existence of an inter-institutional agreement between the student's home and host universities. A maximum total of 12 months per study cycle can be funded. Academic credit for the stay abroad is provided.
montant: The amount of the grant varies according to the country of destination.
duree: 2 to 12 months for each study cycle (Bachelor, Master, PhD)
domainNote: The precondition is the existence of an inter-institutional agreement between the student's home and host universities.

title: Erwin-Schrödinger grants from the Austrian Fonds zur Förderung der wissenschaftlichen Forschung
synthese: The Fonds zur Förderung der wissenschaftlichen Forschung awards Erwin-Schrödinger grants for research programmes abroad during 10 to 24 months.
description: For young and especially highly qualified scientists of any discipline. Objectives of the program: - Promotion of scientific work at leading foreign research institutions; - Gaining experience abroad during the postdoc-phase facilitation of access to new scientific areas, methods, procedures and techniques so as to contribute - following return to Austria - to the further development of science in Austria.
montant: From 45,000 to 62,000 € per year (depending on the destination). For France: 49,300€. Additional benefits: Travel expenses Adjustment of the rate based on the researcher's (family) situation
duree: From 10 to 24 months.
conditions: Eligibility criteria: - Completed doctoral studies - Residence in Austria for at least 3 years within the last 10 years - International scientific publications - Invitation from a foreign research institution - Possibility of returning to Austria after the mobility period All criteria are listed here: https://www.fwf.ac.at/fileadmin/Website/Dokumente/Foerdern/Portfolio/Erwin_Schroedinger/fwf_j_antragsrichtlinien.pdf
inscription: The application has to be done in English via the electronic application portal. Call for application 5 times a year.

title: Financial Aid for Studies Abroad (Studienbeihilfe)
synthese: The Austrian Study Grant Authority (Studienbeihilfenbehörde) provides a supplementary grant to recipients of study grants for study mobilities lasting 1 to 20 months.
description: This is an additional support for grant recipients undertaking a study period abroad for 1 to 20 months. Eligibility requires receiving a study grant. Since the academic year 2019/2020, recipients of study grants participating in ERASMUS+ study mobilities abroad can receive the full ERASMUS+ grant in addition to the Financial Aid for Studies Abroad (rather than just compensatory payment).
montant: Monthly support: €160 or €276 for mobility to France, depending on the grant category of the recipient. Travel expense support: €197 for mobility to France.
duree: Minimum: 1 month Maximum: 20 months
age: Age criteria for receiving the need-based study grant (Studienbeihilfe): Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) must be started before the age of 33. Master's degree or combined master-doctoral program must be started before the age of 38. The reference date is the beginning of each semester.
conditions: Eligibility: Only students already receiving a study grant (Studienbeihilfe) are eligible for this financial aid for studies abroad. Legal reference: § 53 of the Federal Act on the Granting of Study Allowances and Other Study Promotion Measures (Studienförderungsgesetz 1992 – StudFG): Link to the law: https://www.ris.bka.gv.at/GeltendeFassung.wxe?Abfrage=Bundesnormen&Gesetzesnummer=10009824
inscription: Application process: - Submit an application for a study grant in Austria. - Submit an application for financial aid for studies abroad no later than three months after the start of the mobility .
countryNote: For nationality and/or residency criteria, please refer to the Studienbeihilfe website.

title: International student mobility grants - ExcellencES IRIS-E project
synthese: The IRIS-E project supports incoming and outgoing international mobility (to or from one of the project's partner institutions) for undergraduate and master's students with the aim of developing complementary skills related to socio-environmental transition.
description: The IRIS-E project aims to support the challenges of environmental transition by developing interdisciplinary, co-constructed perspectives that promote the transformation of training courses. The IRIS-E team is committed to supporting the outgoing and incoming mobility of students from higher education and research establishments that are part of these perspectives. It is expected that this mobility will enable students to complete their training objectives. Applicants' applications must also meet the IRIS-E criteria: 1) Mandatory link with environmental transition issues ; 2). Link between the project and at least two of the following criteria: a- multidisciplinarity or interdisciplinarity mobilised as part of the mobility. b- new skills targeted, including non-disciplinary skills. c- links between the project and civil society: stakeholders involved in co-construction; participatory science dimensions.
montant: A monthly allowance equivalent to the Erasmus allowance, up to a maximum of 3,000 euros per mobility period.
duree: IRIS-E supports projects lasting from 1 to 6 months.
age: No age requirement. Students from the third year of a Bachelor's degree (Licence 3) to the second year of a Master's degree (Master 2).
conditions: The mobility project must necessarily take place from or toward one of the partner institutions of the IRIS-E project: https://iris-e.univ-rennes.fr/les-partenaires-du-projet Criteria: - The project must be directly related to environmental transition challenges. - The project must also meet at least two of the following criteria: Multidisciplinary or interdisciplinary approaches involved in the mobility project Development of new skills, including non-disciplinary skills Connections with civil society: stakeholders involved in a co-construction process; participatory science dimension
inscription: A student applies for IRIS-E financial support as part of the procedure of their home institution by completing the form provided by their institution, or, if no institutional form is available, by filling in the IRIS-E online form.
pieces: - A cover letter including the positioning of the mobility project in relation to the IRIS-E criteria; - A reflection on the carbon footprint of the travel; - A provisional budget specifying the funding requested and secured: template available on the IRIS-E website; - An invitation letter signed by the director of the host research unit and by the designated contact person responsible for hosting the PhD student, specifying the dates of the stay; - A student ID card or enrolment certificate attesting to the applicant's registration in a higher education institution; - If already established, a copy of the signed internship agreement.
selection: 4–5 incoming mobility projects and 4–5 outgoing mobility projects per year for the Rennes site. Axis 3 of the IRIS-E programme is responsible for selecting applications on a rolling basis as they are received.
countryNote: Europe or outside Europe.
domainNote: The mobility project must be related to environmental transition challenges and develop interdisciplinary and co-constructed perspectives.
levelNote: Criteria: - The project must be directly related to environmental transition challenges. - The project must also meet at least two of the following criteria: Multidisciplinary or interdisciplinary approaches involved in the mobility project Development of new skills, including non-disciplinary skills Connections with civil society: stakeholders involved in a co-construction process; participatory science dimension

title: Chateaubriand Fellowship Program - Embassy of France in the United States
synthese: The Embassy of France in the United States awards grants of €1,400 to €1,500 per month to PhD students.
description: Scholarships for research in France on: [1] humanities and social sciences : French literature, cinema, the humanities, the arts, history, philosophy, political sciences; [2] basic or applied research in science and technology.
montant: €1,400 or €1,500 per month + travel expenditures and assistance in France
duree: [1] Fellowship in social sciences lasts 4 to 8 months (starting date on October 1st or February 1st). [2] In science and technology, the fellowship lasts 6 to 10 months (shouldn't start later than January).
maitriseLangue: Good command of French
conditions: Co-sponsorship by a candidate's American university or French host institution is encouraged.
inscription: Candidates must obtain a letter of recommandation from their advisors in the US and a letter of invitation from a French professor employed in a French university or a research institution.
pieces: List of publications List of past fellowships received List of degrees received, place and date List of other fellowships for which you are applying 3-5 page proposal describing your thesis project 10 line summary IN FRENCH of your thesis subject All contact information from host university An official transcript from each college or university that you have attended. A letter of agreement from your advisor in the United States. One letter of recommendation from a reference who knows your work but who is not your US or French advisor. An invitation letter from a professor in France.
selection: Evaluation by both French and American sholars, then French-American jury
countryNote: Candidates must be enrolled in an American university and they cannot be French citizens.
levelNote: Be enrolled in a PhD course (not finishing during the fellowship year).

title: mobiklasse.de-Lektor:in
synthese: Viens vivre en France pendant dix mois pour faire découvrir ta langue et ta culture aux élèves de tout niveau scolaire !
description: Tu es germanophone et tu as entre 20 et 30 ans ? Tu témoignes d'un bon niveau de français et d'un goût pour l'animation ? Deviens animatrice ou animateur mobiklasse.de en France pour donner envie aux jeunes de découvrir la langue et la culture allemandes !Lors d'une année de césure ou à la fin de tes études, tu te consacres à temps plein à cette mission. En tant qu'animatrice ou animateur mobiklasse.de, tu parcours pendant 10 mois une région de France pour y échanger avec des élèves de tous niveaux. À travers des jeux et des activités ludiques, tu leur transmets l'envie d'apprendre le français.Tu peux organiser tes déplacements et tes activités très librement. Tu bénéficies d'une formation approfondie avant d'aller rencontrer les classes, puis tu bénéficies de formations tout au long de l'année. Tu auras ainsi l'occasion de faire connaissance avec les autres animatrices et animateurs mobiklasse.de.
funder: Foreign organisations, International and bilateral organisations, Regions and cities
montant: En plus de ce soutien pédagogique, l'OFAJ t'attribue une bourse de 1 300 € par mois pendant ton séjour en France et il subvient à tes frais de déplacement et tes frais pédagogiques. Tu bénéficies d'un suivi personnalisé grâce à un tutorat au sein de ton institut de rattachement et d'un suivi avec l'équipe de coordination. Le programme met également un véhicule de service à ta disposition pour une durée de 6 mois pour tes déplacements professionnels.
duree: Dix mois, de septembre à juin
maitriseLangue: Attester d'un niveau B1 de langue française
conditions: Être titulaire du permis de conduire (permis B)
inscription: Les candidatures peuvent être déposées jusqu'au 31 mars 2026 sur notre formulaire en ligne.

title: PROCOPE - MEAE,MESR / DAAD
synthese: The aim of this programme is to develop scientific and technological exchanges of excellence between German and French research laboratories by promoting new collaborations and the participation of young researchers.
description: Since 1986, the Procope programme has supported the development and intensification of research cooperation by encouraging new projects and the participation of young researchers. Procope is a ‘Partenariat Hubert Curien' (PHC) on the French side and a project-based exchange programme (PPP) on the German side. In France, it is funded by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs (MEAE) and the Ministry of Higher Education and Research (MESR) and implemented by Campus France. In Germany, it is funded by the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) and implemented by the Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst (DAAD). The call for applications is aimed at researchers working in higher education establishments or research institutes. Young researchers must be among the participants. Projects run for two years, during which short exchanges (maximum 50 days for the German team and 30 days for the French team) take place between France and Germany.
montant: Accommodation package: Between €89 and €130/day Travel allowance: Between €235 and €400 for the return journey
duree: 2 years, during which short exchange visits (maximum 50 days for the German team or 30 days for the French team) between France and Germany take place several times.
age: No minimum age indicated but reserved for young researchers
maitriseLangue: No need to master the partner's language
inscription: attache-science.berlin-amba@diplomatie.gouv.fr
pieces: More information to follow. https://www.wissenschaft-frankreich.de/procope/
selection: Eligible projects will undergo a separate scientific evaluation in both countries. The authorities in the two countries will then meet to compare the assessments and jointly decide on the funding of the selected projects. On the French side, the Délégation aux Affaires Européennes et Internationales (DAEI) of the MESR is responsible for the scientific evaluation of the applications.
countryNote: Groups of French and German researchers
domainNote: All scientific fields are eligible for funding.

title: Scholarship for training in radio documentary at the ENS Louis Lumière Paris
synthese: This scholarship program is intended for Indian students or young professionals wishing to learn to write and produce radio documentaries (writing, recording, editing and mixing)
description: The French Institute in India offers a scholarship to support the candidature of a student or young Indian professional to undertake an intensive training in the making of radio documentaries at the ENS Louis Lumière Paris, with the support of the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (MEAE)
montant: a living allowance of 920 euros per month, a return ticket and the status of French government scholarship holder entitling them to receive the benefits such as assistance in finding an affordable student accommodation, visa fee waiver, medical insurance etc.
duree: 5 weeks
age: More that 18 years of age at teh time of application
inscription: The applicants must download the application form made available on the Campus France India website and send it to the following address before the deadline: Ms. Kahini Kuchinad at kku@ifindia.in
pieces: Documents to be attached to this form: CV (1 page) (in English) A cover letter (in English) explaining the various reasons why you are applying for this workshop (1 page) A 1-page synopsis of your current sound-based project (if relevant) An ID photo in digital format, to be inserted at the top of the initial page of this
selection: A prior selection of candidates according to the quality and consistency of their profiles.

title: Engineering double-diploma scholarship
synthese: The engineering double-diploma scholarship program is aimed at master's-level engineering students of Moroccan nationality enrolled in an engineering school taking part in the national common exam (CNC).
description: This program awards scholarships to Moroccan students enrolled in a Moroccan engineering school wishing to pursue a double-diploma course at a French engineering school, with which the Moroccan engineering school has a double-diploma agreement that recognizes mobility in France as an integral part of the student's curriculum. At the end of this program, students are expected to receive both a Moroccan engineering diploma and a French engineering diploma. There is no scholarship to cover the compulsory internship period. This French government scholarship cannot be combined with any other scholarship.
montant: - Scholarship of €860/month for the duration of the engineering training course in France (approximately 17 months) - Free visa - Reimbursement of Campus France procedure fees - Social security coverage for the duration of the stay in France - Exemption from tuition fees for establishments under the authority of the MESR - Assistance in finding accommodation in a CROUS university residence
conditions: - Be of Moroccan nationality - Be enrolled in a double-diploma Master's-level engineering program (Moroccan diploma and French diploma at the end of the program) - Excellent academic record - Priority fields
selection: Each Moroccan CNC engineering school pre-selects a maximum of 3 applications from among its students. The shortlisted students must come from at least two different fields of study, in order to present a variety of profiles. The joint selection committee's criteria will focus on : - the student's academic excellence (the first three semesters of the engineering cycle will be considered); - the training specialization: this must fall within one of the specializations likely to meet the needs of the Moroccan job market and the major orientations of bilateral cooperation; - the award of a double diploma: the cooperation agreement between the two establishments will be analyzed to determine whether it explicitly provides for the award of Moroccan and French engineering diplomas.

title: Bourse France Excellence (French Government grants) - French Embassy in North Macedonia
synthese: The French Embassy in Skopje offers every year grants for Masters in France
description: For French and English speaking candidates with a very good application and having chosen the study programs in the fields considered as a priority for the development of the country.
montant: Monthly allowance is 860 euros. Only the registration fees for public universities are covered by the grant. Grantiees might pay in addition tuition fees depending of university.
duree: The duration of the grant covers 2 semesters for Master 1 or Master 2.
age: Macedonian citizenship 30 years maximum * Priority will be given to courses in French. Requests from students with an academic background of excellence for specific courses in English will be examined.
maitriseLangue: A very good knowledge of French is required (minimum level B2) for applications to Masters in French Language
inscription: A proof of a contact for an enrolement in a french university must be part of the application.
pieces: Application form Photocopy of an identity document (passport or identity card); Certificate of pre-registration in Masters ; Transcript of grades and copy of the last diploma obtained (if the originals of the documents are in Macedonian or another language, a certified translation into French is required); Letter of recommendation Motivation letter in which the candidate explains his choice and the way in which he will concretely reinvest the benefit of his studies upon his return to the country; Certificate of the level of French (not mandatory but gives added value to the application); Curriculum Vitae Photograph.
selection: Pre-selection process is based on the quality of the applications and can be followed by an interview.
domainNote: Priority is given to the study programs considered as priority fields for the development of the country and its European integration process.
levelNote: Priority is given to Master level

age: not more than 30 years at the time of the application
maitriseLangue: Knowledge of French is an asset but not mandatory

Scanned copies of marksheets and/or passing certificate of XII, Bachelor's and Master's degrees (including those of completed semesters or the ongoing degree). French language certificate (DELF/DALF)Document(s) of employment / internship record, if any. Recommendation letter(s) Statement of purpose

title: France Excellence Slovénie - High level scientific stay scholarship
synthese: The French Institute of Slovenia offers annual High Level Scientific Stay scholarships for doctoral and post-doctoral students.
description: The French Institute of Slovenia publishes an annual call for applications for high-level scientific scholarships to enable Slovenian doctoral and post-doctoral students to finance a study stay in France.
montant: Scholarship for 1 to 2 months (stay must take place before 31 December 2025): €1704 per month for young researchers, €2055 per month for senior researchers Assistance from Campus France with reception in France and accommodation Social security and civil liability cover Return travel between the nearest international airport and the destination city of your host establishment Cultural and sports activities at preferential rates
duree: Scholarship of 1 to 2 months.
age: Open to doctoral students, young researchers and senior researchers.
conditions: Be of Slovenian nationality (the scholarship is not open to applicants with dual French nationality); Be currently a doctoral student, or have defended a thesis within the last 5 years; Have an invitation from the French host organisation; This call is open to all fields of research; Not be receiving another grant (Erasmus, Ad Futura, etc.) for the duration of the stay; Applicants who have already received a High Level Scientific Residence grant are not eligible for a new grant.
inscription: The call for applications and the application form (in French and in English) for the High Level Scientific Stay are published every year in January on the website of the French Institute of Slovenia (https://www.institutfrance.si/stipendije-za-raziskovalno-bivanje-na-visoki-ravni.html). Applicants must fill in the application form (in French or in English) and return it, with the required documents, to the Attachée for Academic and Scientific Cooperation of the French Institute of Slovenia, by e-mail, before the deadline indicated (25 April 2025).
pieces: a photocopy of an identity document (passport or ID card) ; a curriculum vitae in French or English, indicating publications in international peer-reviewed journals (in ".doc" or ".pdf" format); a cover letter in French or English outlining the research project and the relevance of mobility in France a letter of invitation from the director of the French host organisation, in French or English; a letter of authorisation from the director of the Slovenian home organisation, written in French or English, if the applicant is currently employed in a Slovenian public or private research organisation or in a Slovenian higher education establishment a photocopy of the employment contract from the Slovenian organisation of origin if the candidate is employed; optional: a copy of the DELF/DALF certificate.
selection: The results will be sent to candidates by email in May.
domainNote: All research areas are eligible.
web1: French Institute of Slovenia - High Level Scientific Stay Scholarships

title: France Excellence Slovénie Scholarships - French Institute of Slovenia
synthese: The French Institute of Slovenia offers bachelor's and master's scholarships amounting to €860 per month.
description: The French Institute of Slovenia publishes every year a call for applications for France Excellence Slovénie scholarships to enable Slovenian students at Bachelor or Master level to finance a study stay in France.
montant: - €860 grant - Possibility of access to accommodation in university residence, subject to availability of places - Return travel between the nearest international airport and the destination city of your host establishment - Social security cover and civil liability covered - Full exemption from tuition fees at most public institutions (only for students enrolled at a public institution) - Exemption from the student and campus life contribution (CVEC)
duree: - Scholarship of €860 per month for a period of 10 months (September 2025 - June 2026) for undergraduate students and students entering the 2nd year of a Master's degree in France; - Scholarship of €860 per month for a period of 22 months (September 2025 - June 2027) for students entering the 1st year of a Master's degree in France (subject to continuing their studies in France in the 2nd year of a Master's degree).
maitriseLangue: Proficiency in French and/or in English is required depending on the study project.
conditions: - Be of Slovenian nationality (the scholarship is not open to candidates with dual French nationality); - Be enrolled in a regular Bachelor's or Master's degree course in France in a French higher education institution with the objective of obtaining a degree issued by this institution; - Not to benefit from another scholarship (Erasmus+, Ad Futura...) for the same period of study; - Current and former French government scholarship holders are not eligible for a new scholarship.
inscription: The call for applications and the application form (in French and in English) for the France Excellence Slovénie scholarships are published every year in January on the website of the French Institute of Slovenia (https://www.institutfrance.si/studij-v-franciji.html). Applicants must fill in the application form (in French or in English) and return it, with the required documents, to the Attachée for Academic and Scientific Cooperation of the French Institute of Slovenia, by e-mail, before the deadline indicated (25 April 2025).
pieces: - a copy of an identity document (passport or ID card) ; - a curriculum vitae in French or English (maximum 2 pages, including any publications) ; - a letter of motivation in French or English, setting out the applicant's background and personal and professional objectives (maximum 1 page); - a letter of pre-admission or, failing that, a letter of intent/interest from the French host establishment; - a copy of diplomas obtained since the Matura (inclusive) and a copy of transcripts for the previous two years of study, accompanied by a translation into French or English; - optional: a copy of the DELF/DALF certificate (certifications of French as a foreign language).
selection: Candidates shortlisted on the basis of their applications will be invited to an interview, which will take place in May at the Institut français de Slovénie. The results will be sent to candidates by email between the end of May and mid-June.
domainNote: All fields of study are eligible.
web1: French Institute of Slovenia (France Excellence Slovénie Bachelor-Master)

title: French government scholarships - The French Institute of Bulgaria
synthese: French Government scholarships are awarded within the framework of a competition organized each year by the French Institute in Bulgaria
description: The choice of candidates is made according to priorities defined by the jury, which brings together French and Bulgarian officials. This jury is sovereign and itself determines its selection criteria. BGFs are awarded for degree courses at license (L1), master (M2) and doctorate (joint supervision) level as well as for high-level scientific stays (SSHN) - doctoral students, young researchers, confirmed researchers.
montant: Monthly allowance paid to scholarship holders: 860 € for licenses and masters, 1770 € for cotutelles, 1704 € for SSHN - doctoral students and young researchers, 2055 € for SSHN - confirmed researchers Other costs covered by the French government: - social Security - training and registration fees (1000 € maximum, with some exceptions) - transport costs within French territory to reach the city of assignment
duree: License - 10 months Master -10 months Cotutelle - 3 stays of 4 months in France SSHN - half month or 1 month
age: Age limit: 18 years for the license (L1), 35 years for the master (M2), 40 years for the thesis co-supervision, SSHN doctoral students and young researchers - under 40
maitriseLangue: Knowledge of the French language adapted to the requirements of the university or the field
inscription: Application form to download from the IFB website - www.institutfrancais.bg, section "French Government Bursaries" File to be submitted to the Scholarship Office at the French Institute in Bulgaria by email at the address: bissera.kolarova@institutfrancais.bg
pieces: - application form - Photo - copy of identity card - curriculum vitae - motivation letter presenting the project and the candidate's objective - copy of the diploma of secondary / higher / doctorate studies or transcript, if the diploma is in the process of being obtained - letter of recommendation - letter from the French establishment attesting to the admissibility of the file To add for thesis co-supervision: - thesis co-supervision agreement, signed between the two French and Bulgarian institutions - certificate of registration for the doctoral student's thesis in Bulgaria
selection: Pre-selection on file Publication of the pre-selection results - end of April Interview of preselected candidates with a Franco-Bulgarian jury in May.
countryNote: - be of Bulgarian nationality or have been resident in Bulgaria for more than 3 years - be regularly enrolled in a Bulgarian higher education institution or hold a Bulgarian diploma (bakalavăr, master, doctorate) - for young researchers - be attached to a Bulgarian university or scientific research center - for confirmed researchers - hold a teaching post, researcher in a Bulgarian university or scientific research center
domainNote: All areas
levelNote: Depending on the level of training requested

title: French + Scholarship - The French Embassy in Australia
synthese: Embassy scholarship to support students from Australia wishing to undertake a short programme in France to discover French language and culture, and study various domains.
description: The French Embassy in Australia supports Australian students by offering them a full scholarship for those enrolled in one of the French+programmes. The French+ programme offers 3- to 4-week stays organised by FLE Centres under the "Qualité FLE" label. The sessions are offered in several cities in France. Each session focuses on a specific scientific theme, with all new offerings for 2025: Focus on Energy and Decarbonisation: New Challenges for Society (Montpellier) Marine sciences and technologies (Brest) Micro, nano and smart technologies for industrial applications (Besançon) Focus on transport and energy (Rouen) French + Gastronomy (Rouen) French + Outdoor Sports (Savoie Mont-Blanc).
montant: Students will be covered for the costs of the programme, with accomodation, food and plane tickets included.
duree: 4-6 weeks
maitriseLangue: Students do not need to demonstrate any level of French to enrol.
inscription: To apply for the scholarship, please complete the application form linked below. The completed form and all required documents should be sent to education.canberra-amba@diplomatie.gouv.fr. Deadline for applications: 15 April 2025.
pieces: Please attach the following when submitting: 1. An up-to-date Curriculum Vitae 2. Copies of your academic transcripts and/or qualifications; (if applicable) evidence of current enrolment 3. Copy of Passport 4. (If applicable) Proof of studies in French language / French language certification / evaluation
countryNote: Students must be studying in an Australian higher education institution, or recently finished/enrolling soon. There are no restrictions on nationality.
domainNote: Students in all domains are accepted. The program may benefit students in particular domains, so applications should specify how the scholarship and program will help in that respect.
levelNote: All year levels accepted.

title: The French Government scholarships - The French Institute in Serbia
synthese: In order to promote the mobility of Serbian students in France, the French Embassy and the French Institute in Serbia launched their scholarship program for studies in France
description: In order to foster the mobility of Serbian students to France, The French Embassy and the French Institute in Serbia launched a new scholarship program for studying in France in French or in English for 2025/2026 intake. Every year more than 650 Serbian students choose France in order to continue their studies within 3500 French higher education institutions. Choose your studying program and apply for the French Government scholarship before March 30th, 2025! Given a large number of applications and the rigorous selection, applicants are recommended to submit their applications simultaneously to the other scholarship programs in order to increase their chances of financing their mobility to France. Follow our Instagram page @campusfranceserbie. We post all the scholarship programs for studying in France. Institut français de Serbie Zmaj Jovina 11, 11 000 Beograd mail: vesna.adamovic@institutfrancais.rs phone: 011 / 302-3639 Campus France Serbie bureau mail: sandra.elezovic@institutfrancais.rs Phone: 011/302-3657 Follow our local website www.serbie.campusfrance.org LinkedIn : Campus France Serbie / Studije u Francuskoj Instagram : campusfranceserbie
montant: These scholarships cover living costs in France, the social security and tuition fees of the State Universities. Selected students have the status of the French Government scholarship holder (BGF) offering them other advantages (such as housing, etc.).
duree: 10 months maximum
age: 30 years for the Master 2 level and 35 years for joint-PhD program
maitriseLangue: A good command of French and / or English is mandatory. At the request of the jury, the candidates may be advised to take a language knowledge test allowing them to improve their language level before leaving for France. However, exceptions are made for students wishing to enroll in the programs taught in English.
conditions: Application criteria 1) Quality of the university documents 2) Adequacy with the cooperation priorities defined by the French Institute in Serbia 1. Priority given to the scientific and technical disciplines, but also to the areas related to the climate change and gender equality. 2. Priority given to the projects carried out within the framework of the existing or ongoing institutional cooperation. 3) Quality of the university and professional project 4) Fluency in French and / or English A good command of French is desirable. However, the exceptions are made for the students wishing to enroll into the programs taught in English. 5) Existence of co-financing Particular attention is paid to the applications for which the students foresee another source of funding 6) Quality of the chosen study program
inscription: Please note: Registration to the higher education institutions in France (universities, grandes écoles, etc.) is separate from the scholarship application procedure. Students must pay attention to the deadlines for applying and registering to the chosen course. It is advises to select several courses in France, in case the registration is not accepted to the primary chosen study program.
pieces: 1. curriculum vitae in French (or English); 2. cover letter in French (or English); 3. detailed description of the course that the student wishes to enroll in France, the name of the French higher education institution issuing the chosen diploma, the exact name og the study program, duration, and tuition fees; 4. copy of the last diploma obtained; 5. last transcript of grade obtained; 6. any element that the student deems useful to provide in support of his file (other diplomas, recommendations from professors, etc.); 7. proof that the contact has been previously established with the chosen university (s) or the institution (s) of higher education (s). Note: For documents n˚4 to n˚6, translations into French are not compulsory.
selection: The files are examined by the University and Scientific division of the French Institute in Serbia. Any incomplete or ineligible application is eliminated. A pre-selection on the basis of criteria 1 and 2 exposed below is carried out. Candidates whose applications are preselected are invited for an interview with a jury end of May
domainNote: Even though all the disciplines are eligible for the French Government scholarship program for Master 2 and joint PhD, priority will be given to the applications related to the following scientific topics: - Agribusiness, agriculture, nutrition - Health and epidemiology - New technologies, IT and the industrial engineering - Humanities and social sciences
levelNote: Master 2 and joint PhD program

title: Scholarship - The Programme d'Études en France (PEF) / DAAD
synthese: The Programme d'Études en France (PEF) is aimed at German students for whom French plays an important role and enables them to spend their first study period in France in their second Bachelor year. There are four French partner universities to choose from.
description: [EN] The French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, through the French Embassy in Berlin, in cooperation with the German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD), has launched a new Programme d'Études en France (PEF) for German students in the second year of their Bachelor's degree. This programme is aimed at students for whom French plays an important role and enables them, with a scholarship, to spend a semester at one of four French universities ( Université de Picardie Jules Verne (Amiens), Université de Lille, Université de Nantes or Université Toulouse Jean Jaurès). [DE] Das französische Ministerium für Europa und Auswärtige Angelegenheiten hat über die Französische Botschaft in Berlin, in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Deutschen Akademischen Austauschdienst (DAAD), ein neues Programme d'Études en France (PEF) für deutsche Studierende im zweiten Jahr ihres Bachelor-Abschlusses gestartet. Dieses Programm richtet sich an Studierende, für die Französisch eine wichtige Rolle spielt und ermöglicht es, mit einem Stipendium, ein Semester an einer von vier französischen Universitäten zu verbringen ( Université de Picardie Jules Verne (Amiens), Université de Lille, Université de Nantes oder Université Toulouse Jean Jaurès)
montant: [EN] The funding period is one semester and includes a monthly partial scholarship instalment of 370€. Students are also exempt from tuition fees at the French university and receive health, accident and personal liability insurance benefits. In addition, the PEF provides educational and logistical support for the students. The host university assists with student accommodation. [DE] Die Förderdauer beträgt ein Semester und beinhaltet eine monatliche Teilstipendienrate von 370€. Die Studierenden werden außerdem von den Studiengebühren an der französischen Universität befreit und erhalten Leistungen zur Kranken-, Unfall- und Privathaftpflichtversicherung. Darüber hinaus bietet das PEF eine pädagogische und logistische Betreuung der Studierenden. Die Gastuniversität unterstützt bei der Unterbringung der Studierenden.
duree: [EN] 1 Semester (5months) [DE] 1 Semester (5 Monate)
maitriseLangue: [EN] Candidates must be able to follow lessons in French and participate in study groups. They must also be able to write papers and give oral presentations in French. The required language skills should correspond to level B2 and must be proven. The language certificate must not be older than 1 year [DE] B2 Niveau, nicht älter als 1 Jahr
conditions: [EN] Students must be enrolled in the 2nd year at a German university or higher education institution [DE] Studierende müssen im 2. Jahr an einer deutschen Universität oder Hochschule eingeschrieben sein
inscription: online

title: Tahtawi Master scholarship Program - Embassy of France in Egypt
synthese: The Tahtawi scholarship is a mobility scholarship from the French government managed by the French Embassy in Egypt, which is primarily intended for French-speaking Egyptian students at Master 2 level.
description: The scholarship is restricted to students applying for second year master's program with courses in France. It is possible to benefit from the scholarship during an internship if the internship is mandatory and included in the official program of your Master 2. It is not possible to benefit from the scholarship for an internship only. The scholarship covers only the internship mandatory minimal duration as certified in your study program. The scholarship covers 10 months maximum in total (studies + internship or research). Any extension of the internship period will be at the student own expenses. Application period: December 15th to February 15th, 2025 (at 23:30 GMT +2)
montant: This French government scholarship includes the following benefits: - A monthly stipend of 860 euros for a period of up to 10 months in France (study period and mandatory minimal duration of your internship) ; - an exemption from tuition fees if you study in a public higher education institution, up to a maximum of 5000 €;‎ - access to an accommodation in a student residence (at your expense).‎ - social and health insurance. The scholarship does not cover the travelling fees. If you already had a Tahtawi scholarship, you cannot be selected once again. You can only get the Tahtawi scholarship once.
duree: Application period: December 15th to February 15th, 2025 (at 23:30 GMT +2)
maitriseLangue: - Level of English AND / OR French, certifications accepted : - DELF, DALF, TCF, IELTS, TOEIC certifying at least a B2 level (CERL) - French Baccalaureate, IGCSE, IB, GRE, GED, SAT, AP - Certificate from the candidate university stating that his studies were taught in English and / or French
conditions: Conditions of eligibility - Egyptian nationality (French-Egyptian dual nationals are not eligible) - Study project: application in a Master 2 (2nd year). - Graduated from an Egyptian or French higher education institution (university, schools etc.) OR last year before graduation, certifying that the candidate has followed undergraduate studies for at least 4 years (Bac+4). - Level of English AND / OR French, certifications accepted : - Certificate from the candidate university stating that his studies were taught in English and / or French
inscription: Step 1: apply to one or several master program (2nd year) in France Step 2: complete the information form : https://forms.office.com/r/LYU3D8rN29 Step 3: prepare and combine the documents below. title: The Hubert Curien PHC Tassil Program
synthese: The Hubert Curien PHC Tassili partnership supports Franco-Algerian scientific cooperation
description: The Hubert Curien partnership (PHC Tassili) + is an Algerian-French cooperation program which provides support for joint research projects for a period of 3 years, in particular on mobility within French laboratories, Algerian doctoral students, and young teacher-researchers preparing for accreditation on the one hand, and on the mobility of confirmed French and Algerian researchers between France and Algeria on the other hand. This scientific mobility program focuses on Algerian-French projects relating to food security, energy security, citizen health, artificial intelligence, digitalization, environmental changes and sustainable development.
montant: The average amount of support provided to each project each year is around €20,000: - The French side contributes around €10,000 (on average €8,000 for mobility and €2,000 for logistical support), - The Algerian side contributes around €10,000. The financing of PHC projects for the Algerian part is carried out through credits dedicated to Algerian establishments by the MESRS, whether these are mobility or logistical support credits. For the French part, mobility credits are managed by the operator Campus France, and logistical support by the secretariat of the PHC Tassili in France (Ecole Centrale de Lyon).
duree: The duration of each project is 03 years. Project managers benefit from one coordination mission per year lasting 07 days maximum Doctoral students benefit from a scholarship ranging from 3 months to 6 months maximum per year. Post-doctoral researchers benefit from one month of scholarship per year.
maitriseLangue: Fluency in French is required
conditions: Excluded from the call for applications: Teams whose PHC Tassili or PHC Maghreb project is still ongoing in 2023 or completed at the end of 2022. The same team cannot participate simultaneously in several PHC Tassili projects and a project manager cannot be responsible for more than one project ; Projects providing for the mobility of doctoral students aged over 40; Projects providing for the mobility of Algerian doctoral students who have benefited from a scholarship of more than 6 months (PROFAS B+, PNE, ERASMUS or others, etc.). For French project managers, it is no longer necessary to have HDR. The project manager for the Algerian part must be of magisterial rank (class A lecturer or professor).
inscription: Calls for projects are available on the following websites: http://www.campusfrance.org/fr/tassili
countryNote: The PHC Tassili + is supported and co-financed by: France through the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs (MEAE) and the Ministry of Higher Education and Research (MESR); Algeria, through the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (MESRS).
domainNote: All disciplinary fields are eligible. Particular attention will be paid to cross-cutting projects in areas related to: food security, energy security, citizen health, artificial intelligence and its multiple applications, digitalization of the economy, environmental changes and sustainable development. in a context of climate change. Cross-cutting projects relating to the environment and adaptation to climate change and/or involving socio-economic partnerships will be encouraged, whatever the theme chosen.
levelNote: Joint supervision must be encouraged and co-supervision remains obligatory (1 to 2 per project) – the student must be enrolled in the 1st year of a doctorate in Algeria at the time of submitting the project: this is a criterion for project admissibility. The Algerian and French co-directors must agree on the thesis subject(s) and on the parts of the work that will be carried out in each of the two countries according to a well-established schedule. The application file must include a written commitment from the co-directors to set up co-direction or joint supervision.

title: Bourses France-Acadie for Canadian students of the Atlantic provinces
synthese: These scholarships are available to students at universities in Canada's Atlantic provinces (New These scholarships are available to students at universities in Canada's Atlantic provinces (New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and Newfoundland and Labrador) who would like to pursue their studies in France
description: These scholarships are managed jointly by the French government and the Société Nationale de l'Acadie. The France-Acadie scholarships were created following the meeting of the Four Acadians with President de Gaulle in Paris in January 1968. Today they are one manifestation, among many others, of close cultural relations and of a special bond shared by France and Acadie. They are intended for Canadian students who are on a mobility program in France as part of a university exchange program (1 or 2 semesters). The call for proposals is made annually, and the dates may vary.
funder: French government, Foreign organisations, Regions and cities
montant: A France-Acadie Scholarship may cover, in part or in full, within the limits of the allocated budget - International transportation from Atlantic Canada to France and back; - Transportation in Canada from your place of residence to the airport; - Transportation in France from the airport to the study site; - Transportation and accommodation to Montreal for visa purposes.

maitriseLangue: An intermediate (Level B2) proficiency in French is required (TCF, TEFAQ, DELF).

pieces: Mandatory supporting documents: - the completed application form in French (to be downloaded annually from the website of the Consulate General of France in the Atlantic Provinces or the Société Nationale de l'Acadie); - an up-to-date curriculum vitae; - a letter of motivation explaining the training project and the professional project (2 pages maximum); - certificate of pre-registration or letter of acceptance in the study institution in France; - a completed certificate of non-holding of French nationality (model in the form to be downloaded) Optional supporting documents: - Letter(s) of recommendation - transcript(s) of grades
selection: The jury consists of representatives of the Société Nationale de l'Acadie and the Consulates General in the Atlantic Provinces. Four primary aspects will determine the jury's choice: - the applicant's motivation; - the applicant's intention to return and contribute to the development of the francophonie in Canada's Atlantic provinces.

synthese: At the Master's level, Quebec students can benefit from the Frontenac scholarship program.
description: The objective of the programme is to facilitate the mobility to France of Quebec students enrolled in a Master's programme in all sectors. The applicant is : - enrolled full-time in a bidiploma master's programme at a Quebec university and a French university or - admitted or in the process of applying for admission to one or more full-time, onsite master's programmes in France or - will be studying in France as part of an exchange program between a Québec university and a French university, an exchange that will be credited towards their master's degree. title: France Excellence Master Programme
synthese: France Excellence Master (FEX) is a scholarship program supported by Agence Campus France and the French Embassy in Singapore that allows students enrolled in a Master's program in France to benefit from a scholarship (BGF).
description: Did you know that France is a country of innovation and cutting edge technology that is applied not only in science but also in its gastronomy, fashion and art de vivre? The country that gave the world the croissant, haute couture, molecular cooking and discoveries by Pasteur and Curie, now wants to sponsor your studies! If you have been accepted into a Master programme in an accredited French institution of higher learning, congratulations! You will benefit from France's long tradition of excellence in your chosen field, and at the same time feed your inner culture vulture on the staples of the French way of life. A well-rounded education could be your passport to future career and personal success. If you are starting your Master programme around September 2024, we invite you to submit an application. If selected, you will get a scholarship for the duration of your course (24 months maximum) Please do note that : - The scholarship is for a maximum of 24 months. - The scholarship is not compatible with alternance (apprenticeship) or any type of full-time employement contract. Thus, the scholarship cannot cover a course which requires a compulsory alternance. The scholarship remains however compatible with an internship. - The scholarship will not waive tuition fees but only registration rights in public universities fixed by government decree (243 or 3770 euros for a Master's degree) - In order for the plane ticket to be covered, the departure date should be around the start date of your scholarship (about 3 days before the start date of the scholarship, which itself will take place one week before the start of your course)
montant: - Round-trip airfare (at the start and end of the programme) - Health insurance coverage for the entire duration of the Master's program. - Student visa and the cost of the Etudes en France procedure for students. - A monthly allowance in the amount of 860 €/month (≈1250 SGD). - Status of French Government Scholarship Recipient (BGF) All other expenses are the responsibility of the student.
duree: 24 months maximum
conditions: Eligibility criteria: All areas of studies Acceptance into a Master programme in an accredited French institution of higher education* Start of courses in Fall 2024 Keen interest in France and French culture *Acceptance can be pending and students will be granted the scholarship after they can confirmed they have been accepted to the program.
inscription: https://www.singapour.campusfrance.org/applications-for-the-france-excellence-master-scholarships-2024-are-now-open study@ambafrance-sg.org
pieces: Required documents to be sent in a single PDF file: Resume Cover Letter to apply to the scholarship Application form (to be downloaded above) A copy of the highest Diploma obtained A proof of acceptance in a master programme in France* *If the acceptance is still pending, students can provide a proof that they are waiting for a decision from the jury. Please send your application to study@ambafrance-sg.org with the subject "Application for France Excellence Masters 2024" with all the above mentionned documents in a single PDF file, not exceeding 7MB.
selection: Submission of application -> Preselection of candidates Pre-selected candidates interview and jury decision -> Final selection

title: Research award - PHC Germaine de Staël
synthese: Germaine de Staël is the Franco-Swiss Partenariat Hubert Curien (PHC). It is implemented in Switzerland by SATW and SEFRI, and in France by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs (MEAE) and the Ministry of Higher Education and Research (MESR).
description: The aim of this programme is to develop scientific and technological exchanges of excellence between laboratories and research teams in the two countries, by encouraging new cooperative ventures. All scientific fields, including the humanities and social sciences, are covered by this programme. Particular attention will be paid to projects whose themes are related to those of the Horizon Europe framework programme for research and innovation. The call for applications is open to tenured researchers in research laboratories attached to higher education establishments or research organisations. Companies may participate in the project, provided they are associated with an academic partner. Only applications co-submitted by the partner researchers to the authorities responsible for managing the programme in their respective countries will be accepted. Project leaders from French teams must ensure that their partners have also submitted their applications. Projects that have already received support under this programme are not eligible for a new application immediately after their completion.
montant: The amount covers only the cost of mobility between the two countries for the researchers involved in the programme, by reimbursing travel and subsistence expenses. Any other funding required to implement the joint projects will have to come from the partner laboratories' own resources or from other sources. The funds can only be used to travel to the partner country (Switzerland). The overall budget for French applicants is €2,400/year. Overnight stays are capped at €180/night. Travel is capped at €500. Several exchanges are possible during the year.
duree: Funding is granted on an annual basis, for two consecutive years. It must be used between 1 January and 31 December of the year in question and cannot be carried over to the following year. Renewal of credits for a second year is subject to : Submission of a progress report outlining the scientific results obtained and the mobility activities carried out or planned before the end of the current year (one page in free format); Drawing up a financial report on the actions carried out or planned before the end of the calendar year; Optimum use of funding granted for the first year. The progress report and financial statement must be sent to the French Embassy in Switzerland by 15 September of the first year.
age: There is no age limit, but the active participation and mobility of young researchers, particularly doctoral and post-doctoral students, is one of the main selection criteria.
conditions: Other evaluation criteria should also be taken into account: The scientific quality of the project; The quality and competence of the French and foreign teams; The value of the cooperation and the complementary nature of the French and foreign teams; The prospects for structuring or developing the project; Priority will be given to networked projects with a European dimension; Particular attention will be paid to projects that fit in with the European Union's political priorities as expressed in the new Horizon Europe framework programme. A final scientific and financial report is required no later than three months after the end of the projects. Project leaders from French teams must use the downloadable report template and attach it to their online application by this deadline. This report must also be sent to the French Embassy in Switzerland by the same deadline (see programme contact). Project leaders are invited to inform the French Embassy in Switzerland if they obtain funding (particularly European funding) to continue the project within 3 years of the end of the Germaine de Staël Partnership, as well as any publications resulting from this partnership. Publications produced as part of this project should mention the support granted by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs (MEAE) and the Ministry of Higher Education and Research (MESR).
inscription: The submission procedure for the French section is entirely online on the Campus France website. Swiss applicants must submit a parallel application to SATW. Publication of the call for projects: 11/03/2024 Deadline for co-submission of applications: 15/05/2024 Publication of results on the Campus France extranet: November-December 2024 Start of 2025 projects: January 2025 Project sponsors are invited to submit their applications early to avoid technical problems that could compromise the timely submission of their applications; Applications may be submitted in French or English.
selection: The two countries' authorities meet, alternately in Switzerland and France, to compare the assessments and jointly decide on the support to be granted to the selected projects. On the French side, the MESR's Delegation for European and International Affairs (DAEI) is responsible for the scientific evaluation of the projects.
countryNote: Project managers are responsible for taking all necessary steps to protect intellectual property.

title: France Excellence Descartes - Embassy of France in the Hague

description: More than 150 students from all Dutch universities have already had the opportunity to study or do an internship in France thanks to the Descartes Excellence Grants. In addition to the monthly allowance, for a period of 10 months (3 or 4 months for internship scholarships), the scholarship status also covers student social security and part of the university tuition fees. The scholarship holder is assisted throughout his/her stay in France and remains in close contact with the Embassy services. TYPES OF SCHOLARSHIPS -10-month scholarships for students who have obtained at least a Bachelor's degree in the Netherlands and wish to follow a Master's degree in France -2 or 3 month internship scholarships for students preparing a PhD in the Netherlands and wishing to carry out a research internship in a laboratory in France PROFILE Student with at least a Dutch Bachelor degree, but priority will be given to students with a Master degree or higher. Fluency in French: this will be assessed according to the chosen course and the language of tuition. All disciplines are concerned Priority will be given to applications with a link to MOPGA themes APPLICATION - Form to be downloaded online https://institutfrancais.nl/nl/open-calls/descartes-studiebeurzen/ - Motivation letter specifying how the study project in France fits in with the student's academic and professional career - CV with photo - Copies of university diplomas and transcripts - Two letters of recommendation from a teacher or professional - Certificate of enrolment or acceptance if you have already been contacted or accepted by a French higher education institution

title: France Excellence Van Dongen - Embassy of France in The Hague
synthese: The van Dongen scholarships support Art and Design graduate students from a Dutch university who wish to pursue a Master in a French art school.
description: Since 2001, more than 140 students from a wide array of Dutch higher education institutions had the opportunity to either study or intern in France, thanks to the selective scholarships offered by the Institut Français des Pays-Bas. In French institutions recognised for the high quality of teaching, these students could further their education in a variety of disciplines. The van Dongen scholarships are aimed at students in Art or Design, who have a well-defined, coeherent and motivated plan to study in France. Thus, it is imperative to research the different opportunities to study in France before sending in an application to the scholarships.
montant: - Monthly allowance of approx. 700 € per months for ten months. - Tuition fees of the French high education institution are covered for up to 5000 €, as well as social security. - Multiple bonuses are awarded to scholarship-holders by the French government (accommodation financial support, student life, etc.).

conditions: The applicant is responsible for applying to, and any additional administrative procedures regarding the chosen French higher education institution. The final attribution of the scholarship will only come into effect after the selected recipient has been accepted into a French art school. The van Dongen artistic scholarship cannot be cumulated with other scholarships awarded by the French government, Agence Française de la Francophonie scholarships, or the Erasmus+ programme. The recipients of the scholarship commit to attend the course that the scholarship was attributed to them for; to regularly keep the Institut Français des Pays-Bas informed of the progress of their stay in France; participate in promotional activities for the mobility scholarships and the France Alumni Pays-Bas network when they come back.
