title: The Royal Golden Jubilee (RGJ) PhD Programme
synthese: The Royal Golden Jubilee (RGJ) is a prestigious scholarship programme funded by the Royal Thai Government. The programme was launched in 1996 to increase the number of PhD graduates and improve the quality and quantity of research for the sustainable development of the nation.
description: The Royal Golden Jubilee (RGJ) Excellence Programme was established in 1996, with the aim of achieving four main objectives : to increase the number of PHDs in science and technology in Thailand (i), to produce a significant number of international publications (ii), to promote research between Thailand and its foreign partners (iii) and to strengthen doctoral training in Thai universities (iv). This programme has already enabled nearly 300-400 Thai students (usually selected from the best - top 10% of a class for 60% of them) to obtain a scholarship for their doctoral studies. The National Research Council of Thailand (NRCT) is a Thai research funding agency in charge of the RGJ programme. This agency plans to support the student's research work with two professors, one Thai and one foreign. In this context, nearly thirty Thai universities have entered into relations with more than 1000 universities and laboratories, located in 49 countries around the world, by requesting the intervention of nearly 3,700 foreign professors. The Royal Golden Jubilee (RGJ) programme between France and Thailand allows for the joint financing of doctoral scholarships, with the aim of strengthening scientific exchanges between France and Thailand. The objective is in particular to create Franco-Thai centers of expertise in scientific research, in compliance with intellectual property rules. In this context, the French Embassy in Thailand provides funding, allowing Thai students to extend their stay in France by 3 to 6 months.
montant: - The benefits included in the programme are : travel, free consular fees, social security/insurance, living allowance, training costs and language preparation before their departure to France. - The amount of the living allowance is 1500 euros per month.
duree: These scientific stay grants are awarded for a maximum period of 6 months and may exceptionally be extended to 9 months subject to authorization from the Embassy of France in Thailand.
maitriseLangue: A very good level of English or French (C1 level is recommended)
conditions: Each student is required to produce at least one international publication before graduation.
inscription: - Step 1 : Doctoral advisors form public or private Thai universities who wish to apply for RGJ-PHD scholarships must send the Foundation the duly completed PK 2.2/49 forms and the loaded diskettes (which can be sent by email as attachments). - Step 2 : Grant applicants will be evaluated on the basis of their research records, research grants received and the strength and seriousness of their collaborators abroad. The results of the scholarship awards will be announced on the TRF and RGJ-PHD websites. - Step 3 : Qualified PHD students who wish to apply for a research assistantship in the RGJ-PHD programme should apply directly to the PHD advisors who have received an RGJ-PHD scholarship in Step 2 above. Successful students will receive the first installment of the grants.
pieces: The proposal should not exceed four A4 pages using Times New Roman format, font 12, including : Thesis (Thai and English) The type of scholarship (RGJ-Industry/RGJ - Frontier Research/RGJ for Humanity, Social Sciences, Liberal Arts and Environment) The specified user of this research work (private sector/social ministry/department/organization) The problem statement and motivation The keywords (3-5 keywords) The literature reviw The research objectives The research methodology The scope of the research The expected product, outcome and impact of the research work The research framework (mind map) that shows the link between impact, outcome, outputs, process and inputs should not exceed one A4 page.
selection: - The advisor must fill out an online application form and submit the proposal and research framework on the RGJ webpage (http://rgjadvisor.trf.or.th). - The student must fill out an online application form for "ASEAN student" on the RGJ webpage (https://rgjasean.trf.or.th/)
countryNote: To be citizen of one of the ASEAN countries (Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Vietnam, Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos and Brunei) Excellent academic results (bachelor's degree and master's degree) To be able to pursue full-time doctoral studies in Thailand (3-5 years) have published research work or made oral or poster presentations at a scientific meeting with an abstract in English.
domainNote: The research topic may be a specific request for solutions in the humanities, social sciences, liberal arts of environment, formulated by a ministry, a department or an organization. The research topic may also be related to key issues such as : - Inequality and poverty education ; - Creative learning and education reform ; - Good governance and corruption reduction ; - Climate change ; - Water management ;
levelNote: The student must obtain " First Class Honours " or " Second Class Honours " in his or her Bachelor's and Master's degree. To ensure that academic performance meets international standards, only PHD advisors with good research records and co-advisors or collaborators in recognized universities abroad will be eligible for the Royal Golden Jubilee (RGJ) Excellence Programme.
web1: The Thailand Research Fund under the Royal Thai governement

title: "Women in Mathematics" scholarships
synthese: The FMJH is launching a scholarship program designed to encourage young women to take up mathematics, starting in the third year of a Bachelor's degree. The students concerned are those planning to study for an L3 degree (third year of Bachelor) on the Paris-Saclay campus.
description: The scholarships offered are L3+M1+M2. This means that grants awarded in L3 will be automatically renewed in M1 and then in M2 if the student successfully pursues her studies in the Master's program in mathematics and applications co-accredited by the University of Paris-Saclay and the Institut Polytechnique de Paris. A jury selects the winners according to criteria defined by the FMJH Scientific Council, with excellence at the top of the list. As the aim of this program is to encourage talented young women to pursue mathematics at least as far as a Master's degree and even a PhD, candidates are asked to take particular care in writing up their study project in their application.
montant: €11,000 net per year; Allowance to cover university registration fees; Lump-sum contribution of up to €2,000 per year foreign students according to country of origin to cover travel expenses for one round trip per year as well as visa fees.
duree: The scholarships offered are L3+M1+M2. This means that grants awarded in L3 will be automatically renewed in M1 and then in M2 if the student successfully pursues her studies in the Master's program in mathematics and applications co-accredited by the University of Paris-Saclay and the Institut Polytechnique de Paris.
age: All female students wishing to enroll in L3 at Université Paris-Saclay or Institut Polytechnique de Paris are eligible. All applications are examined.
maitriseLangue: French or English depending on the L3 course concerned
conditions: Letters of recommendation are automatically requested to the referees indicated by applicants as soon as their application has been validated. inscription: You can apply online.
pieces: Transcripts from each institution previously attended during the first years of the Licence or equivalent. Academic CV; Names and addresses of two referees; A study plan.
selection: The selection process is carried out by a jury appointed by the FMJH steering committee, in agreement with the heads of the L3 courses concerned. The results are sent by e-mail to the winners around 5 weeks after the closing date for applications.

title: Scholarships for international students in research-oriented master's programmes - University of Rennes Foundation
synthese: As part of its efforts to promote international openness and excellence in research, the Fondation Université de Rennes invites applications from international students who wish to continue their studies at Masters 1 or 2 level at the University of Rennes and who meet the criteria of excellence.
description: Scholarships for international students - University of Rennes Foundation Are you an international student wishing to pursue your Master's studies in France? The University of Rennes would be delighted to welcome you to its campuses! In 2026, the University of Rennes Foundation is renewing its call for applications to welcome international students wishing to pursue their studies in a Master's 1 or Master's 2 programme at the University of Rennes for the 2026-2027 academic year, with the aim of pursuing a career/training in research. title: Entente Cordiale scholarships
synthese: Entente Cordiale scholarships are available to British postgraduate students applying for a Master's degree in France.
description: Entente Cordiale scholarships are available to British postgraduate students wishing to study in France. Created in 1995 by French President Jacques Chirac and British Prime Minister John Major, the programme aims not only to enable students to study in France, but also to promote exchanges between tomorrow's decision-makers in France and the UK. These exchanges are facilitated by the Entente Cordiale Alumni network: made up of students, researchers and sponsors, this influential network offers students who join strong career development opportunities. Students must apply for a Master's programme in their chosen field of study, for a period of six months at least. They should present in their application an ambitious project contributing to the strengthening of Franco-British relations.
montant: 700 euros per month
duree: 6 to 12 months
pieces: - Copies of all your degrees including A-Levels - Two university references - Acceptance letter or application file - Curriculum vitae - Course description
selection: - Academic excellence - Relevance of the professional project - Participation of the project in strengthening Franco-British relations.
countryNote: Only UK residents are eligible (any nationality, except French).
domainNote: Any field of study.

title: Master Scholarships - CIHEAM Montpellier
synthese: CIHEAM Montpellier offers scholarships to the top candidates admitted to a Master's programme at our Institute. These scholarships are intended exclusively for applicants from a CIHEAM member country (Albania, Algeria, Egypt, Spain, Greece, Italy, Lebanon, Malta, Morocco, Portugal, Tunisia, Turkey).
description: Are you looking to deepen your knowledge, acquire dual expertise, or gain international exposure? CIHEAM Montpellier can help you bring your project to completion by offering Master 2 training programmes dedicated to the challenges of sustainable development in agriculture, rural areas, and agrifood systems . Scholarships are available for the top candidates from a CIHEAM member country (Albania, Algeria, Egypt, Spain, Greece, Italy, Lebanon, Malta, Morocco, Portugal, Tunisia, Turkey). At CIHEAM Montpellier, an intergovernmental institute where all nationalities come together, we offer dynamic teaching, an active learning approach, and support from an international team of teacher-researchers. In addition to field trips carried out as a group, a 3- to 6-month individual internship will allow you to put your knowledge into practice and gain initial professional experience. This internship can be completed in France or abroad. Not fully proficient in French? The CFLE was created specifically for you! The Centre for French as a Foreign Language offers intensive French language courses to help you reach the required level and follow one of the three Master's programmes taught in French.
montant: The CIHEAM Montpellier scholarship covers: Tuiton fees Health and hospital insurance Student and Campus Life Contribution (CVEC) Accommodation at the CIHEAM Montpellier residence (individual room in a shared studio – possibility of a single studio with the additional cost to be covered by the student) Additional allowance for living expenses in Montpellier Costs to be borne by scholarship recipients: Registration fee: 250 euros Round-trip travel Meals
duree: 7 months
maitriseLangue: Minimum required level in French (for the CGAT, CDVALES and ECODEVA Master's programmes): B1.2 (having completed at least 400 hours of French courses), according to the criteria of the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR) for languages. Minimum required level in English (for the MIDAS Master's programme): B1.2 (having completed at least 400 hours of English courses), according to the criteria of the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR) for languages.
inscription: Applications for the Master 2 programmes at CIHEAM Montpellier and for the scholarship are submitted online : Online application form to be completed Supporting documents to be uploaded via the application form
pieces: Completed application form Resume Highest post-graduate/university degree Transcripts from higher education studies (preparatory cycle, Bachelor's degree, Master's degree, engineering cycle, etc.)
selection: The admission requirement is a minimum of 4 years of higher education after the Baccalaureate (equivalent to 240 ECTS) in the fields of economics, human sciences, or agronomy. Professional experience is valued. A selection committee composed of CIHEAM Montpellier academic staff reviews the applications and ranks candidates according to the quality of their files (grades obtained, academic background, acquired skills, etc.). Candidates meeting the required academic criteria are invited to selection interviews, held either in person or remotely depending on the chosen Master's programme and the candidate's country of origin. Candidates selected after the interviews will be invited based on the number of available places. Invitation letters will be sent out in June. In the event of withdrawal, additional candidates may be invited from the waiting list.
countryNote: Scholarships intended for candidates from a CIHEAM member country (Albania, Algeria, Egypt, Spain, Greece, Italy, Lebanon, Malta, Morocco, Portugal, Tunisia, Turkey).
domainNote: Agronomy, economics, geography or sociology
levelNote: To be eligible for admission to CIHEAM Montpellier, you must hold a minimum of a four-year university degree (equivalent to 240 ECTS)

title: Mistral Excellence Scholarship - Avignon Université
synthese: The Mistral excellence scholarship program is intended for international students of an excellent level enrolled in a Higher Education Institution outside France and who wish to pursue their studies at Avignon University in order to obtain a Master's Degree.
description: The Mistral excellence scholarship program is intended for international students of an excellent level enrolled in a Higher Education Institution outside France and who wish to pursue their studies at Avignon University in order to obtain a Master's Degree.
montant: 6 000 euros for the first year of the scholarship 6 000 euros for the second year
duree: 1 year renewable according to program criteria
age: To be under 28 years old on the 31 December 2026
maitriseLangue: French B2 minimum, C1 for some Master's Degrees
conditions: - To be enrolled in Higher Education Institution outside France when applying (applicants enrolled in a Avignon University's partner Institution will be prioritised); - To have a very good academic record and meet the academic and linguistic criteria established by the faculty of the Master's Degree at Avignon University; - Not to have interrupted their studies for more than an academic year; - To apply for an enrollment in the 1st or 2nd year of a Master's Degree at Avignon University for the 2025-2026 academic year; - Not to have a residence in France; - To be under 28 years old on the 31 of December 2025; - Never have applied for a Mistral scholarship (except in the case of a renewal); - Not to benefit from another scholarship for the requested Master's Degree. Applying for the Mistral program does not exclude applying for another scholarship application in parallel with the Mistral application. In case of obtaining a scholarship other than the Mistral scholarship, the candidate must inform Avignon University as soon as possible and renounce the Mistral scholarship.
inscription: Applications must be submitted through the online platform. Application deadline: 23 March 2026
pieces: - A certificate of enrollment in a Higher Education Institution outside France at the time of the application (or of the previous academic year for candidates who have interrupted their studies for less than a year); - Copies of all diplomas obtained since the end of high school; - Copies of all the transcripts of records obtained during higher education together with a description of the grading system used in the country of origin; - Proof of the candidate's level of French (minimum B2 level); - A letter of recommendation from a professor at the applicant's home university; - A letter of motivation in French in which the candidate explains the choice of the Master's Degree at Avignon University, also specifying his/her professional project; - An updated curriculum vitae in French; - The CEF identifier for students who are nationals of the countries concerned by the CampusFrance procedure.
selection: A commission is charge of examining the applications and selecting the scholarship winners. Successful applicants will then receive a confirmation letter. The commission is sovereign in its deliberation and cannot be contested.
levelNote: To have an excellent academic level

title: French Government Scholarship
synthese: The "Institut français d'Autriche" and the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs offer Excellence Scholarships "Séjours Scientifiques de Haut Niveau" for short research stays (1 to 6 months) as well as for doctoral studies (in the framework of a cotutelle or co-direction agreement).
description: The "Institut français d'Autriche" and the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs offer Excellence Scholarships "Séjours Scientifiques de Haut Niveau" for short research stays (1 to 6 months) as well as for doctoral studies (in the framework of a cotutelle or co-direction agreement). These are intended for talented doctoral students, post-docs and young researchers who have obtained their thesis less than 5 years ago and are working in an Austrian and/or French research institution (university, research centre, etc.). This mobility should allow young researchers to deepen their research in France, in order to set up new cooperations. The duration of the stay can vary from 1 to 6 months. The grants are reserved for Austrian doctoral students and young researchers (post-docs or researchers with a thesis less than 5 years old at the date of arrival of the grant holder in France) or those residing in Austria and registered in an Austrian and/or French higher education institution or research centre. Short research stays and doctoral studies may be conducted in English provided that the supervisor specifies in his or her letter that the mobility student's host university agrees that the studies or short research stay may be conducted in English.
montant: 1700€ per month.
duree: 1 to 6 month(s).
maitriseLangue: Knowledge of French is an asset but not a necessity.
inscription: Timetable and selection procedure : Applications must be sent by e-mail to vienne@campusfrance.org before 20 March 2026. Applications are received at the French Institute of Austria and examined by the scientific and university cooperation service. The best candidates will be invited in April to an interview before a jury of academic experts. Candidates will be informed of the results between the end of April and the beginning of May.
levelNote: PhD obtained less than 5 years ago for postdocs applying.

title: French+Sciences Programm - Embassy of France in Slovakia
synthese: The French Embassy in Slovakia offers grants to participate in short scientific stays "French+Sciences", to simultaneously discover France and the French language, and learn some science in English.
description: The French+Sciences programme offers undergraduate students a three- or four-week stay in France to discover innovative themes around current issues in English. Possible thematic stays are: Focus on sustainable development, Languedoc ( June 4 to 24, 2025) Science and technology of the sea, Bretagne (June 19 to July 7, 2025) Micro , nano & smart technologies for industrial applications, Franche-Comté (June 5 to 30, 2025) Focus on transport & energy, Normandie (May 29 to June 16, 2025). In addition to these scientific presentations, the programme includes French language courses (all levels), site visits (companies or research centres) and tourist excursions. All information on the French+Sciences programme is available here in English: https://ressources.campusfrance.org/esr/cours_sejours/en/brochure_french+Sciences_en.pdf
montant: The grant will cover the costs of training, accommodation and travel.
duree: 3-4 weeks
maitriseLangue: have a minimum level of B2 in English all levels of French (including beginner) are accepted
inscription: Applications must be sent by e-mail to the attention of Ms Martina Saganová (martina.saganova@institutfrançais.sk) before 20/03/2025.
pieces: a completed application form, template to be downloaded here: https://institutfrancais.sk/veda-a-univerzity/stipendia/pre-studentov/ a letter of motivation in English presenting your interest in the programme as well as your study and/or professional plans a curriculum vitae letters of support (e.g. from your teachers) may optionally be attached to the application form

title: IBioS master scholarship - EUR IMCBio
synthese: The IMCBio Graduate School offers funding for research internships and mobility assistance (installation & travel expenses for students from outside Strasbourg) by joining the IMCBio Graduate School.
description: Starting in September 2025, the IMCBio Graduate School will open a new dedicated Master international track: Integrative Biological Sciences (IBioS) as part of the Life Science Master Mention at the Life Science Faculty of the University of Strasbourg. The IBioS international course in Integrative Biological Sciences aims to train students in research through research, by placing them as early as possible in an immersive and professionalizing environment, in connection with the inherent societal, ethical and socio-economic issues. To foster this immersive experience and maximize the international appeal of the program, all courses and activities will be taught in English. To have more information about our Master track, please refer to our website (https://imcbio.unistra.fr). Each year, the IMCBio Graduate School will train around 16 students as part of their master's course at the University of Strasbourg, including funding support for internships. Three disciplinary internships are scheduled over the two years of the Master's program: two two-month internships in M1 and one five-to-six months internship in M2, all funded by the Graduate School. Internships are carried out in the laboratories of excellence of the “Institut Thématique Interdisciplinaire” (ITI) IMCBio+ (http://imcbioplus.unistra.fr). Students for this excellence Master program are selected competitively on their achievements and motivation based of their undergraduate transcripts, a letter of motivation, and a resume.
montant: Stipends of around 600 Euros per month are provided during internships. Additional support is available for students doing an internship abroad (assistance with travel and accommodation costs). Mobility assistance (installation & travel expenses for foreign students) may be granted to students joining the IMCBio Graduate School from abroad after evaluation of their application.
duree: Funding for Master 1 and Master 2 internships is guaranteed for students enrolled in the IMCBio Graduate School.
maitriseLangue: Proof of proficiency in English (B2), basic level in French (A2) is not required but may be a plus.
conditions: If a mobility grant is awarded, 100% of it is paid on signature of the arrival certificate. In addition, the IMCBio Graduate School reserves the right to demand full reimbursement of support if the course is not completed by the student.
inscription: Applicants must register for a Master's degree on the French government's ‘Mon Master' website (https://www.monmaster.gouv.fr) (exact dates not yet defined) and/or on Campus France for “Etudes en France” countries. Funding from the IMCBio Graduate School can be combined with grants based on social criteria, but some cannot be combined with the following support schemes: - Unistra international mobility support scheme (DRI) - Erasmus+ MIC / Mundus / KA 103 except Erasmus+ Internship KA103 - UFA - Other financial support from IdEx funding for the same academic year.
pieces: Your application must include your CV, your Bachelor's degree transcript (or equivalent), and a cover letter (1 page) in pdf format. The CV should describe: - A clear overview of your career path (specialization, mentors, internships, etc.) The cover letter should describe: - Your scientific interests - Why you are an excellent candidate for the IMCBio Graduate School.
selection: Applications are first submitted through the "Mon Master" process for EU applicants or "Mes Etudes en France" for non-EU applicants. Applications are then reviewed by a selection committee. For dates, please refer to the "Mon Master" or "Mes Etudes en France" calendar.
domainNote: Molecular and Cellular Biology Integrative Structural Biology and Bioinformatics Biomedicine Molecular genetics of development and stem cells Immunology and inflammation Microbiology Molecular biology and plant biotechnology Virology
levelNote: Licence/Bachelor degree in life sciences, possibly medicine, physics, chemistry, computing or mathematics with basic knowledge of biology

title: France Excellence Romania – Doctoral Level Scholarship
synthese: Each year, the Embassy of France in Romania and the French Institute in Romania launch a call for applications for Romanian students wishing to pursue doctoral studies in France or in cooperation with a French research laboratory.
montant: A monthly allowance of €1,770 per month* for 4 months per year, for a maximum duration of 3 years, subject to the applicable parameters and the annual budget allocated to scholarships Coverage of health insurance and civil liability Possibility of access to accommodation in a university residence, subject to availability Reception and support during the study stay by Campus France
duree: 4 months per year, for a maximum duration of 3 years.
pieces: Each applicant must submit an application file including the following documents: The duly completed and signed application form A research project (1 to 3 pages) A copy of an identity document (passport or national identity card) A letter of motivation in French (presentation of the research topic and the relevance of a joint doctoral programme with France) A curriculum vitae in French A copy of the Master's degree diploma (in the absence of the diploma, an official certificate of completion issued by the university will be accepted) Copies of academic transcripts for all years of Master's studies A letter of intent from the French research supervisor confirming their willingness to host the candidate, or the joint supervision agreement (cotutelle) if already established One letter of recommendation (optional) A provisional mobility schedule starting from 1 January 2027 A French language test or diploma (DELF/DALF/TCF) (optional) NB: Although not mandatory, a French language certificate at B1 level or above (DELF or TCF) will be considered an asset. The French language proficiency of shortlisted candidates will be assessed and taken into account during the interviews for the final selection.
selection: Phase 1: Pre-selection of applications Applications are received by the French Institute in Romania and reviewed by the University and Scientific Exchange Department. Candidates whose applications are pre-selected will be invited to the French Institute in Romania for a motivation interview. Phase 2: Motivation interview The motivation interview takes place before a joint French-Romanian panel, usually composed of representatives from the French Institute in Romania and Romanian academics. The panel will convene in May 2026 and will assess both the quality of the applications and the candidates' ability to present and defend their study project and professional plan. Phase 3: Announcement of results Candidates who are definitively selected will be informed a few weeks after the motivation interview. They will then be asked to confirm their acceptance of the scholarship.
countryNote: Hold Romanian nationality (the scholarship is not open to candidates holding dual French nationality).
levelNote: Be enrolled in the 1st or 2nd year of a joint doctoral programme (cotutelle).

title: France Excellence Romania – Postdoctoral Level Scholarship
synthese: Each year, the Embassy of France in Romania and the French Institute in Romania launch a call for applications for Romanian researchers. This call is open to postdoctoral candidates until 6 March 2026.
montant: A monthly allowance of €1,704 per month for early-career researchers (less than 5 years since obtaining their PhD) and €2,055 per month for established researchers (5 years or more since obtaining their PhD), for a maximum duration of 2 months Coverage of health insurance and civil liability Possibility of access to accommodation in a university residence, subject to availability Reception and support during the study stay by Campus France

pieces: Each applicant must submit an application file including the following documents: The completed and signed information form A research project (1 to 3 pages) A copy of an identity document (passport or national identity card) A letter of motivation in French (presentation of the research topic and the relevance of mobility to France) A curriculum vitae in French A copy of the doctoral degree diploma A hosting letter from the French research institution A provisional mobility schedule starting from 1 July 2026 (the mobility must be completed before 31 December 2026) A letter of recommendation (optional) A French language test or diploma (DELF/DALF/TCF) (optional)
selection: Phase 1: Pre-selection of applications Applications are received by the French Institute in Romania and reviewed by the University and Scientific Exchange Department. Candidates whose applications are pre-selected will be invited to the French Institute in Romania for a motivation interview. Phase 2: Motivation interview The motivation interview takes place before a joint French-Romanian panel, usually composed of representatives from the French Institute in Romania and Romanian academics. The panel will convene in May 2026 and will assess both the quality of the applications and the candidates' ability to present and defend their research project and professional plan. Phase 3: Announcement of results Candidates who are definitively selected will be informed a few weeks after the motivation interview. They will then be asked to confirm their acceptance of the scholarship.
countryNote: Hold Romanian nationality (the scholarship is not open to candidates holding dual French nationality).
levelNote: Hold a doctoral degree obtained in Romania.

title: France Excellence Romania Scholarship – Master's level
synthese: Each year, the Embassy of France in Romania and the French Institute in Romania launch a call for applications for Romanian students wishing to pursue their studies in France. This call is open to Master's level candidates until 6 March 2026.
montant: Benefits of the French Government Scholarship – Master's level A monthly allowance of €860 Coverage of health insurance and civil liability Possibility of accommodation in a university residence, subject to availability Reception and follow-up during the study period by Campus France
duree: The duration of the French Government Scholarship at Master's level is 10 months.
conditions: Have submitted an application to one or more French universities of their choice. Proof of initial contact with a Master's programme coordinator in France (email exchanges, etc.) will be highly appreciated.
pieces: A duly completed and signed application form A copy of an identity document (passport or national identity card) A cover letter in French outlining the study project A curriculum vitae in French A letter of recommendation (optional) A copy of the baccalaureate diploma Copies of academic degrees obtained (if the diploma is not yet available, an official certificate from the university will be accepted) Copies of academic transcripts from the first year of the Bachelor's degree onward A French language test or diploma (DELF / DALF / TCF) (optional) Proof of initial contact with the requested programme (e.g. screenshots of email exchanges with the Master's programme coordinators) (optional)
selection: Phase 1: Pre-selection of applications Applications are received at the French Institute in Romania and reviewed by the University and Scientific Exchange Unit. Candidates whose applications are pre-selected are then invited to the French Institute in Romania for a motivation interview. Phase 2: Motivation interview The motivation interview is conducted before a mixed Franco-Romanian jury, generally composed of representatives from the French Institute in Romania and Romanian academics. The jury will meet in May 2026. It evaluates both the quality of the application and the candidate's ability to present and defend their study and professional project. Phase 3: Announcement of results Candidates who are definitively selected will be informed a few weeks after the motivation interview. They will then be asked to confirm whether they accept the scholarship offer.
countryNote: Hold Romanian nationality (the scholarship is not open to candidates holding dual French nationality).
levelNote: Have successfully completed three or four years of higher education (Bachelor's level or Master 1), or be currently enrolled in the third year of a Bachelor's degree or in Master 1.

title: Mobility Master 2
synthese: Master 2 level scholarship in a higher education institution in Nouvelle Aquitaine
description: Financing a year at master level 2 in a higher education institution in the region Nouvelle-Aquitaine Countries eligibles : OIF members countries( outside Européan Union) and régional cooperation area (Canada Province du Québec, Maroc Région du Souss-Massa, Sénégal Départements Bambey-Diourbel-Fatick-Foundiougne-Gossas-Mbacké, Burkina Faso Région du Plateau central, Madagascar Région Itasy, Vietnam Provinces Thua Thien Huê-Lao Cai, Chine Province de Hubei)
montant: 6 000 € for one year or 4 000 € for a semester
duree: One Year
maitriseLangue: Yes
inscription: in the higher education institution in Nouvelle- Aquitaine
pieces: the application form completed by the student; A letter of recommendation from the applicant's home institution assessing the applicant's academic quality and adaptability; The planned (balanced) budget for the study year in terms of expenditures (transportation, accommodation, food, registration fees, etc.) and expected revenues (scholarships, personal contributions, etc.); A letter from the host institution in Nouvelle-Aquitaine stating his intention to welcome the student and specifying the training concerned.
selection: higher education institutions sends applications in order of priority The Région Nouvelle-Aquitaine committee examines applications according to various criteria: academic excellence, strategic university partnerships, priority streams and areas of cooperation...

domainNote: no specific criteria.

title: French Government Scholarship - Embassy of France in Slovakia
synthese: The Service of Cooperation and Cultural Action of the French Embassy in Slovakia offers the co-finances scholarship for Slovak students wishing to study in France at the Bachelor's or Master's level (all levels) for an amount of 470 euros/month. The duration is one academic year.
description: Co-financed scholarship (France Excellence 2025) In order to offer more study stays in France, the Embassy offers to Slovak students who can afford it, co-financed scholarship to spend a year of higher education in France. This scholarship offers the student status: (medical insurance, exemption from enrolment fees) as well as a monthly allowance partially covering the needs. Applicants must be able to meet part of their financial needs from their own resources (390 €/month) for the duration of their stay in France. Possible courses - Licence : 3 year course L1, L2 and L3 may include an internship - Master 1: a one-year course, generally without an internship, which can lead to a "maîtrise" degree Many fields of study are concerned by this scholarship: exact and engineering sciences; life and earth sciences; social, legal, political and economic sciences; humanities... The duration of the training must be 10 months maximum. For the academic year 2025/2026 the training can start from September or October 2025.
montant: 470 €/month
duree: 10 months
maitriseLangue: Applicants for French-language studies must have a level of French (B2 minimum) that allows them to present their study project in French for about ten minutes and to answer questions from the selection committee in French. Candidates for English-language studies must have a minimum level of English B2.
conditions: Letter of acceptance It is the responsibility of the applicant for a French government scholarship to choose his/her university in France and to make the necessary contacts to obtain a letter of acceptance. Students can be advised and assisted in this process by their teachers or by the international relations office of their university.
inscription: - Applications must be sent by mail to the attention of Ms Martina Saganová (martina.saganova@institutfrancais.sk, Francúzsky inštitút na Slovensku, Sedlárska 7, 812 83 Bratislava) by February 28 2025 .
pieces: - The application form duly completed - Photocopy of academic transcript (last two years) - Parcoursup" sheet - first wish - Cover letter - CV in French or in English language
selection: - The preselected candidates will be invited to present their applications in front of a selection panel which will take place in April 2025. - Candidates will be informed of the results of this selection during May 2025 and will be able to leave for France from 1st September 2025.
countryNote: The excellence of the application and the coherence of the study project with the professional project of the candidate.

title: Joint supervision thesis scholarships - The French Embassy in Slovakia
synthese: The Department of cooperation and cultural action at the French Embassy in Slovakia offers scholarships to PhD students doing a joint supervised thesis. The amount of the scholarship is 1 690 €/month. The PhD students spends 6 months in France and 6 months in Slovakia each year for three years.
description: Joint supervision of thesis scholarships are French governement scholarships exclusively for Slovak young researchers who wants to do their thesis at the same time in France and in Slovakia. The research work will take place under the joint direction of a French scientist and a Slovak scientist. For three years, the PhD students will spend six months a year in each of the two universities. During his three stays of six months in France, the PhD students will benefit from a scholarship from the French government. Once the candidate is selected, a document called "Joint supervision agreement for thesis" will regulate the modalities of the preparation of the doctorate and define the validity of the diploma.
montant: 1 588 €/month
duree: The thesis is realized in three years (6 months in France, 6 months in Slovakia each year).
maitriseLangue: You can study PhD in France in English as well.
conditions: It belongs to the candidate to the joint supervised thesis scholarship to choose his university in France and make necessary contacts to get an invitation letter. The students can receive advice and help from their Slovak teachers and the office of international relations in their university.
inscription: - Applications must be sent by mail to the attention of Ms Martina Saganová (Francúzsky inštitút na Slovensku, Sedlárska 7, 812 83 Bratislava; martina.saganova@institutfrancais.sk) by February 28 2025.
pieces: Application form Copies of obtained degrees Copies of Academic transcripts for the past two years Research project Cover letter Agreement of both supervisors for a joint supervision Resume in French or English
selection: The preselected candidates will be invited to present their applications in front of a selection panel.
countryNote: The scientific excellence of the application and the prospects of cooperation between the French and Slovak institutions.
levelNote: (Master's degree)

title: Mobility Grant
synthese: For studies pursued entirely in a country of the European Economic Area (EEA), Switzerland, or the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, it is possible to obtain a mobility grant.
description: For studies pursued entirely in a country of the European Economic Area (EEA), Switzerland, or the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, it is possible to obtain a mobility grant. This grant is paid during the first year of study after submitting proof of academic achievement of at least 15 ECTS credits. From the second year of study, the same conditions for favorable academic success as for the study grant (Studienbeihilfe) apply. The proof of success must be provided in German or English. For each semester/trimester, a confirmation of enrollment or admission must be submitted. Note: When calculating the mobility grant, other financial aids and loans for educational purposes must be taken into account. Distance learning programs pursued from Austria cannot be funded by a mobility grant. IMPORTANT: An annual application is required for the mobility grant!
montant: The amount of the mobility grant is calculated similarly to the amount of the study grant for domestic studies, generally based on the rate for students living away from home (€9,024). For a more precise calculation, see "Grant Amount & Calculation Examples": https://www.stipendium.at/stipendien/studienbeihilfe#c390
age: Same Age Criteria as for Study Grant (Studienbeihilfe): - Bachelor's degree or equivalent must have been started before the age of 33. - Master's degree or combined master-doctoral program must be started before the age of 38. The reference date is the beginning of each semester.
conditions: Conditions: - Bachelor's, Master's, or diploma studies must be pursued at a recognized post-secondary educational institution. This grant does not apply to doctoral studies. For German educational institutions, recognition depends on whether they are listed in the Hochschulkompass as having "public sponsorship." For other EEA institutions, as well as those in Switzerland and the United Kingdom, accreditation requires the "H+" status in the Anabin database. - No higher education degree should have been obtained yet. Exception: Despite having completed a Bachelor's degree, a mobility grant can still be awarded for a consecutive Master's program. - The criteria for social eligibility, favorable academic success, and age limit correspond to those required for obtaining a study grant (Studienbeihilfe).
inscription: The application for the mobility grant must be submitted to the Study Grant Authority (Studienbeihilfenbehörde).
countryNote: For nationality and/or residency criteria, please refer to the Studienbeihilfe website.

title: The Franco-Thai scholarship program - Embassy of France in Thailand
synthese: The Franco-Thai scholarship program aims to support Thai students under 35 years of age who intend to study in French universities or higher education establishments, at Master's or PhD level.
description: This call for applications is open to all fields of study. The annual calendar is renewable every year : - Launch of the Franco-Thai scholarship program : November 2025 - Preparatory workshops by Campus France : January 2026 - Online application deadline : February 19th 2026 - Interviews with shortlisted candidates : March 2026 - Publication of first list of laureates : May 2026 - Departure for France : Early September 2026 Scholarship recipients will be contacted individually. The final results will be published online on the Franco-Thai scholarship program website in July. The committee's decisions are unquestionable. The maximum grant is 860 euros per month for the Master's program and 1500 euros per month for the PHD program. To apply, please read the “rulebook” on our website carefully before applying directly: https://www.francothai-science.com/franco-thai-scholarship-program
montant: This program offers two types of scholarships : Full scholarship : - A monthly allowance ; - Round-trip ticket; - Social protection; - Benefits as a French government scholarship holder. Co-financing scholarship : 1) Social Security Grant : This gives access to a specific status , enabling candidates to benefit from social protection in France and other specific advantages. It can only be awarded if a cost-sharing agreement ensures a monthly allowance for the student. 2) Shared-cost scholarship with monthly allowance : Applicants are strongly encouraged to seek other sources of funding , from their own local or foreign university, or from the private sector. Special consideration will be given to applicants who have found other sources of funding.
duree: The Franco-Thai scholarship is awarded for the duration required to obtain the degree : one or two years for a Master's degree and three years for a PhD.
age: You must be under 35 years old.
maitriseLangue: A good level of French OR English is required. The minimum level is B2, but C1 is reached by most selected candidates .
inscription: - The application for the Franco-Thai scholarship program is only possible online, starting in November, and must be completed in full on the Franco-Thai scholarship website: https://www.francothai-science.com/franco-thai-scholarship-program - Applications received by e-mail will not be considered. All applicants must submit their application on the dedicated website.
pieces: The list of documents required to apply : - A completed 2026 scholarship application form (online) ; - A copy of passport/identity card; - An up to date curriculum vitae (CV) including all university studies; - A cover letter explaining the applicant's motivation and interest in the proposed project; - Copies of university diplomas (bachelor's, master's or doctorate only); - Copies of transcripts. For master's degree candidates : Copy of registration certificate. If the application process has not yet begun for the program in question, please include copies of e-mail exchanges with the French university to underline the seriousness of the project. For PhD candidates : - An attestation signed by your tutor indicating his or her commitment to supervise your thesis. - In the case of co-supervision, an attestation signed by both thesis supervisors (Thai and French) indicating their commitment to supervise in France and Thailand. - A detailed description of the research project (2-3 pages) including a detailed work plan; - In the case of co-supervision, a clear and detailed plan of the different periods to be spent in France during the research. Optional documents for all applicants : - A letter of academic or professional recommendation - Cost-sharing agreement - Language proficiency certificates: French (TCF, DELF, DALF etc.) and/or English (TOEFL, TOEIC, IELTS etc.)
selection: The selection process is divided into two distinct phases : - During the first phase of the selection process , applications are examined in detail, taking into account a number of specific criteria, such as academic excellence, the student's career plan and motivations . Candidates whose academic files impress the selection committee are then called for an individual interview. - During the second phase of the selection process , the performance of the candidates during the interviews is evaluated, and those who have convinced the jury are then included on the official list of Franco-Thai scholarship laureates .
countryNote: You must be of Thai nationality.
domainNote: All fields of study are considered.
levelNote: The selection criteria are as follows: - The candidate's skills and merit as demonstrated by his or her academic and professional record . - The quality of the study plan . Contacts with program directors and project progress will be taken into account. - The candidate's interest in pursuing his or her studies in France. - Level of foreign language proficiency ( French or English ). - Other sources of funding to support the studies/project. - For PhD candidates, the selection committee will give preference to co-tutored and co-financed PhDs . The commitment of Thai and French supervisors will be decisive.

title: Scholarship Fondation Générations Solidaires IDHL
synthese: Scholarship for students from southern countries to join the Master's cycle mention "Freedoms Right" of the Lyon Institute of Human Rights (IDHL), at the Catholic University of Lyon.
description: The scholarship of Fondation Générations Solidaires is intended to finance students from developping countries to join the Master's cycle mention "Freedoms Right" of the Lyon Institute of Human Rights (IDHL), at the Catholic University of Lyon (UCLy). The first year course entitled "International and European Human Rights Law" (taught in French) takes place over 10 months from September to June and aims to train lawyers in international and European law (European Union and Council of Europe). The Master 2 offers two courses: - Master 2 Freedom laws - International and regional human rights law in practice (taught in French) - Master's Degree - Human Rights Diplomacy (taught in English)
montant: The scholarship amounts to approximately €9 500 per year. This sum covers the registration fees and part of the living expenses (housing, food, insurance) but personal financing will be essential for the travel expenses to Lyon and the additional living expenses. The facilities granted to the scholarship holder will not extend to the family members who would join him/her. The reservation of a university room is not systematic. The scholarship holder must contact the UCLy accommodation service upon reception of the scholarship notification.
duree: The scholarship is awarded for the first year of the Master (10 months) and renewable for the continuation of studies in the second year of the Master under certain conditions. Direct entry in second year does not allow you to apply for a scholarship.
age: Under 26 at the time of application
maitriseLangue: Most courses are given in French. A good written and spoken knowledge of French language is therefore required. Candidates who have not completed their studies in French must provide a certificate of language skills (Diplôme d'Etudes en Langue Française (DELF), Alliance française, etc.)
conditions: The status of scholarship entails duties: the student is required to respect the duration of the training, as well as the rules of attendance. In case of voluntary interruption of the studies, the scholarship would be suspended. In addition, at the end of the training, the scholarship holder undertakes to return home to apply the knowledge acquired in the promotion and protection of human rights.
inscription: Applications for the scholarship must be made online from mid-December (M1 page, Admission tab) and must be received no later than February 14, 2024. When you obtain your Campus France login, don't forget to put our school in your training basket. Without this identifier, applications will not be processed.
pieces: 1. An ID photo 2. Copy of passport or ID 3. A certified copy of all your original diplomas with their translation into French (established by a sworn translator) 4. A statement of the courses taken and the marks obtained for each of your years of university studies 5. Your baccalaureate transcript or equivalent 6. A cover letter 7. A detailed resume 8. A certificate of knowledge of French if you did not study in French 9. Letters of recommendation from referees (teachers, employers, association leaders) if applicable attesting to your commitment to human rights. Each letter must include the name of the referent, his/her contact details (telephone, fax, email and the official stamp of his institution).
selection: Only complete applications will be considered: - Complete applications submitted on the IDHL website before the deadline. The Institute's Board of Directors will examine the applications and inform applicants of the outcome. In the event of refusal, the application will not be renewed for the following year's campaign. Candidates wishing to apply again must submit a complete application the following year. Candidates must not leave their home country until they have received their letter of acceptance.
countryNote: Scholarship open to students of law and political science
domainNote: Scholarship opened to students with a law degree

title: short-term fellowships Atlas
synthese: The Fondation Maison des sciences de l'homme (FMSH) and the Institut français de Roumanie (IFR) offer 2 short-term fellowships of two months in France for young postdoc researchers from Romania who have presented their thesis from 2020.
montant: Laureates will receive a total stipend of 3 600€ for the two months (2 instalments of 1 800€ paid at the beginning of each month of stay). This financial contribution is intended to cover expenditure such as transport and accommodation costs. Laureates will be considered as “Boursier du Gouvernement Français” and will have access to affordable accommodation, social security for the time of their stay and get a financial support to buy bibliographic material. Laureates will also benefit from free visa and logistical support to organise their stay (possibility to have a workspace, letter for the libraries...).
duree: The Fondation Maison des sciences de l'homme (FMSH) and the Institut français de Roumanie (IFR) offer 2 short-term fellowships of two months in France for young postdoc researchers from Romania who have presented their thesis from 2020.
conditions: French host institution: Before submitting their application, applicants will have to find a French research institution to host them for the time of their stay. Applicants will have to provide a letter from the hosting institution addressed to the FMSH and the IFR expressing the institution's willingness to host the applicant during the time of fellowship and explaining the work conditions offered.
inscription: Applicants will be required to submit an online application form and a scientific dossier (research project + appendices). The online application form will be available on the FMSH website as of october 06th 2025. Completed proposals can be uploaded to the application portal at any time before the application deadline of february 06th 2026, 17:00 (Paris time). Online application and scientific dossier can be submitted in French or English.
pieces: Content of scientific dossier The research proposal: the research proposal should consist in a short presentation from 10 000 characters to 20 000 characters (spaces and references included) composed with: State of art, problematic, objective and specific aim of the research project, methodology. A bibliography The detailed programme of the research stay (places and institutions to be visited, contacts, workplan). Appendices: A Curriculum vitae (2 pages maximum) A list of publications A copy of the PhD diploma A letter from the director of the research institution in Romania A letter of invitation from the director of the host research institution in France expressing the institution's willingness to host the applicant during the time of fellowship and explaining the work conditions they can offer
selection: A selection committee composed with members of FMSH, IFR, CEREFREA-Villa Noël and independent experts will analyse and proceed to final selection of applications regarding the following criteria: The quality of the scientific dossier and the methodology developed The relevance of a research stay in France regarding the scientific project and the candidate curricula The ability to identify scientific contacts in France Candidates that have never benefited from the programme will be prioritized. Candidates will be informed by email of the results from end of march 2026.
countryNote: Nationality/Residence: This program is open to Romania nationals who are affiliated with an institution of higher education and research / institute of research based in the country.
domainNote: Theme: Applicants must be involved in research in social and human sciences .
levelNote: Educational Degree: Applicants must have obtained their PhD doctorate and presented their thesis from 2020.

title: PGSM Master
synthese: The French Embassy in Romania and the Paris Mathematical Sciences Foundation are co-funding two Master's scholarships in the field of mathematics for the 2026–2027 academic year, as part of the PGSM Romania programme. These scholarships offer financial support of €860 per month, along with guidance provided by Campus

title: Maryam Mirzakhani 2026 scholarships
synthese: With the Maryam Mirzakhani doctoral scholarships, the FMJH is pleased to encourage female students from all countries and nationalities to pursue a doctorate in the Paris-Saclay area. 2 scholarships are offered. Open to all female students at the bachelor's or first-year master's level.
description: The FMJH is delighted to offer Maryam Mirzakhani PhD scholarships for female students of any nationality in order to encourage them preparing a PhD within the Hadamard Doctoral School (EDMH). Like the junior Maryam Mirzakhani prizes offered yearly by the FMJH, these scholarships commemorate the life and work of Iranian mathematician Maryam Mirzakhani (1977-2017), who became the first female mathematician to win the Fields Medal, in 2014. To be eligible you should intend to enroll for a Master's degree in "Mathematics and Applications" (M1 or M2) at the Université Paris-Saclay or the Institut Polytechnique de Paris and then prepare a PhD within EDMH. As such, at the time of application, you should be in the process of completing either a bachelor's degree or the first year of a master's degree (or equivalent), preferably in mathematics. The list of eligible courses appears in the drop-down menu of the online application form but you can also find it on our website.
montant: The grant consists of: 1. A master's excellence scholarship (11000€/year) for 2 years or 1 year depending on whether the student plans to enroll in the first or the second year of the master's degree. For all the winners an indemnity covering tuition fees (around €400 for a year). First-time international students also receive a flat-rate allowance of up to €2,000, calculated on a scale based on their country of origin. This lump-sum contribution is intended to cover the cost of one round trip the first year and visa fees. They are also offered the possibility of booking accommodation (individual studio) in one of the residences close to their institution (only Orsay and Evry) as well as a housing welcome KIT containing all the necessary household items to an approximate value of € 100. 2. A doctoral funding commitment for 3 years (a total minimum gross funding of approximately €82,800 over 3 years, following the rules established by the French ministry of higher education and research).
duree: The scholarship covers the master's years of the laureate as well as doctoral funding commitments with a monthly salary.
maitriseLangue: If you are not a French speaker, you are invited to follow the M1 Jacques Hadamard tracks in Orsay or Ecole Polytechnique, which include a coherent and comprehensive program of courses taught in English. In addition, in the second year of the master's program, you will find a wide range of courses taught in English covering the entire spectrum of mathematics. It should also be noted that the Sophie Germain scholarship comes with access to French language courses, as even a basic command of French is useful for getting the most out of your years of study in France.
conditions: Any students applying to Master's degree "Mathématiques et applications" of the Université Paris Saclay or Institut Polytechnique de Paris is eligible (apart from the track "Formation à l'Enseignement Supérieur en Mathématiques"). All applications are considered. The scholarship cannot be combined with any other excellence scholarship. In case of doubt, please contact the FMJH (contact@fondation-hadamard.fr). It is strongly recommended for candidates outside Europe to submit their application as part of first call for applications to facilitate the processing of their visa. Similarly, it is imperative that they take contact with their Embassy or Consulate to obtain a CAMPUS France file number. The selection of candidates is done on academic criteria confirmed by transcripts and recommendation letters. Recommendation letters are requested automatically by the FMJH to the contact persons mentioned by the candidates as soon as they validate their application. Regarding the enrollment's formalities of students in the Master's track of his choice, it is imperative that all candidates for a scholarship proceed in parallel to their registration online via the website of the Université Paris-Saclay or Institut Polytechnique de Paris.
inscription: Applications must be submitted using the online form available on our website.
pieces: - CV - Transcripts and degrees - Study plan - One or two email addresses of a professor from their home institution who is able to provide a letter of recommendation (an email will be sent automatically explaining how to submit the letter of recommendation).
selection: All applications will be examined impartially and without discrimination of geographical origin, according to the criteria of excellence defined by the Scientific Council of the FMJH. The selection is made by a jury appointed by the FMJH steering committee and in agreement with the heads of the Master's courses and tracks concerned. The award jury will make a preliminary selection among the applications. The applicants selected at this stage will be interviewed by videoconference in English or French, depending on their preference. The results are sent by e-mail to the laureates about 5 weeks after the closing of applications.

title: SOPHIE GERMAIN MASTER'S SCHOLARSHIPS 2026
synthese: The Mathematics Foundation Jacques Hadamard (FMJH) is offering a number of one or two years scholarships for talented students applying for a Master Study "Mathematics and Applications" in one of their member institutions at Université Paris-Saclay or Institut Polytechnique de Paris.
description: The Mathematics Foundation Jacques Hadamard (FMJH) is offering scholarships for a period of one or two year(s) for French and foreign students. The institutions members of the FMJH are supporting the Master "Mathematics and applications". The Sophie Germain Scholarships are intended for students who want to enroll in one of the programs (apart from the track "Formation à l'Enseignement Supérieur en Mathématiques") of this master. A jury selects the laureates applying the criteria defined by the Scientific Council of the FMJH, the main selection criterion being excellence. Since this program aims to encourage young talents to orientate themselves towards research in mathematics, applicants are asked to give careful attention to the writing of their motivation letter in their file. This call is synchronized with the 2026 Maryam Mirzakhani call for applications dedicated to female students who intend to prepare a PhD at the EDMH after the Master's degree in "Mathematics and Applications" (M1 or M2) at the Université Paris-Saclay or the Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Your application will be automatically reviewed and if you are shortlisted, you will be invited to an interview to obtain a Maryam Mirzakhani doctoral scholarship.
montant: The amount of the award amounts to €11,000 net per year. Is added to the purse for all the winners an indemnity covering tuition fees (€400 for a year). First-time international students also receive a flat-rate allowance of up to €2,000, calculated on a scale based on their country of origin. This lump-sum contribution is intended to cover the cost of one round trip the first year and visa fees. They are also offered the possibility of booking accommodation (individual studio) in one of the residences close to their institution (only Orsay and Evry) as well as a housing welcome KIT containing all the necessary household items to an approximate value of € 100. Except in exceptional cases, the scholarship cannot be cumulated with any other excellence scholarship. In case of doubt, please contact the direction of the FMJH (contact@fondation-hadamard.fr).
duree: 1 or 2 years for master's degree
maitriseLangue: If you are not a French speaker, you are invited to follow the M1 Jacques Hadamard tracks in Orsay or Ecole Polytechnique, which include a coherent and comprehensive program of courses taught in English. In addition, in the second year of the master's program, you will find a wide range of courses taught in English covering the entire spectrum of mathematics. It should also be noted that the Sophie Germain scholarship comes with access to French language courses, as even a basic command of French is useful for getting the most out of your years of study in France.
conditions: Any students applying to Master's degree "Mathématiques et applications" of the Université Paris Saclay or Institut Polytechnique de Paris is eligible (apart from the track "Formation à l'Enseignement Supérieur en Mathématiques"). All applications are considered. It is strongly recommended for candidates outside Europe to submit their application as part of first call for applications to facilitate the processing of their visa. Similarly, it is imperative that they take contact with their Embassy or Consulate to obtain a CAMPUS France file number. The selection of candidates is done on academic criteria confirmed by transcripts and recommendation letters. Recommendation letters are requested automatically by the FMJH to the contact persons mentioned by the candidates as soon as they validate their application. Regarding the enrollment's formalities of students in the Master's track of his choice, it is imperative that all candidates for a scholarship proceed in parallel to their registration online via the website of the Université Paris-Saclay or Institut Polytechnique de Paris.
inscription: Each academic year, two calls are successively launched for the upcoming year: The first call is from October to January 31st. It is intended to encourage incoming mobility within the Paris-Saclay area and therefore only concerns students outside this area. Note that international students (outside Europe) must apply for a visa on Campus France. The second call is from February to May and concerns only the "insiders", i.e. the students who already study on the territory of Paris-Saclay.
pieces: - CV - Degree certificates and transcripts - Study plan - One or two email addresses of a professor from their home institution who is able to provide a letter of recommendation (an email will be sent automatically explaining how to submit the letter of recommendation).
selection: All applications will be examined impartially and without discrimination of geographical origin, according to the criteria of excellence defined by the Scientific Council of the FMJH. The selection is made by a jury appointed by the FMJH steering committee and in agreement with the heads of the Master's courses and tracks concerned. The results are sent by e-mail to the laureates about 5 weeks after the closing of applications.

title: CENTRALE NANTES - Consortium Scholarship: Electric Vehicule Propulsion and Control (E-PiCo+)
synthese: As E-PiCo+ Master holds the Erasmus Mundus label of excellence, the higher ranked students (after eligibility check and academic selection) can beneficiate from a tuition fee waiver.
description: E-PiCo+ is a 2-year Master programme that offers useful and necessary multidisciplinary topics in the e-mobility field. E-PiCo+ will provide technical and scientific solutions to the issue of fossil consumption and greenhouse gas emission. It is devised to train students in the field of e-mobility in order to have them work towards ecological transition . It is directly applicable to industry by training future electric propulsion system expert graduates. Through lectures by reputable researchers, practical work on the latest experimental platforms, sessions with industrial specialists, annual workshops, E-PiCo+ students acquire the most advanced knowledge that will prepare them for the upcoming challenges in e-mobility. E-PiCo+ is an integrated Master's course designed and conducted by partners institutions sharing a common vision of electric vehicle propulsion and control: - Centrale Nantes, France (coordinating institution) - Universita Degli Studi dell'Aquila, Italy - Christian-Albrechts-Universität Zu Kiel, Germany - Universitatea Națională de Știință și Tehnologie, Romania - Centro de Investigación y de Estudios Avanzados del Instituto Politécnico Nacional (CINVESTAV), Mexico Students graduating from the E-PiCo+ Master's course are awarded two (or three) Master's degrees from the institutions where they studied, as well as a Diploma Supplement. The degrees obtained are officially recognized and give full access to PhD study programmes. Tuitions fees: Partner country students (Non-European Union): €18 000 for 2 years Programme country students (European Union and related countries): €9 000 for 2 years
montant: Consortium scholarships Consortium scholarships are available to European and Non-European students applying as self-funded , as a reduction of the tuition fees from 50% up to 100%.
duree: 2 years
maitriseLangue: The applicants have to be fluent in English, both written and spoken. An applicant whose native language is not English is required to pass a recognized international English test: - TOEFL (CBT 220, PBT 550, IBT 80), - Cambridge English Test (B2 or higher), - IELTS (6.5 or higher), - TOEIC (800 or higher). No other test is recognized.

title: Margaret McNamara Education Grants
synthese: Margaret McNamara Education Grants (MMEG) is a nonprofit, public charity founded in 1981 that awards education grants to women from developing countries who are at least 25 years old and enrolled at universities in France.
description: MMEG is a public, nonprofit charitable organization whose mission is to improve the lives of women and children by supporting the higher education of exceptional women from developing countries who will become catalysts for change. Since 1981, MMEG has been dedicated to empowering women by supporting their education so they can build a better world. Grant recipients have focused on a wide range of fields, including engineering, information technology, health, science, education, social sciences, and law. However, there are no restrictions regarding fields of study. The scholarship is open to all women, or those who identify as women, from developing and middle-income countries who intend, after completing their degree, to work in or with a developing country to improve the lives of women and/or children.
montant: As part of its France Program, MMEG awards one-time, non-renewable scholarships of USD 5,000.
duree: The scholarship, in the amount of USD 5,000, is awarded as a one-time, non-renewable grant.
age: Identify as a woman and be at least 25 years old by the application deadline.
maitriseLangue: The language for applications to the France Program is French: application forms must be completed in French, and selection interviews are conducted online in French.
conditions: Candidates must meet the following additional eligibility criteria: They must not be related to an employee, spouse, or retiree of the World Bank Group, International Monetary Fund, Inter-American Development Bank, or a member of the MMEG Board of Directors. MMEG only considers complete applications. Any application form must be submitted with ALL required documents. Missing or invalid documents at the application deadline will result in disqualification, meaning the candidate will be automatically excluded. Scholarships are awarded to women from developing and middle-income countries who intend, after graduation, to work in or with a developing country to improve the lives of women and/or children. We encourage MMEG scholarship recipients to share information about our scholarship with other students and to build networks with fellow recipients. In addition to the general eligibility criteria listed above, each candidate must: Be already enrolled as a full-time student with the appropriate student visa in their national passport OR residence permit; and Plan to continue full-time studies in the following academic semester.
inscription: In the application form, you will provide: A brief description of your personal story, as well as the connections between your studies, experiences, and future projects, and the commitment you demonstrate to women and children in developing countries. An estimate of your financial situation, including anticipated expenses for the upcoming academic year, and the strategies you plan to use to cover your funding needs. A summary of your thesis (if applicable), including its objective, methodology, and expected results, as well as the relationship between the thesis and your career goals. Two letters of recommendation are required.
pieces: Please scan the documents listed below (PDF format preferred, or JPEG/PNG) before beginning to fill out the application form: Photo ID: (a) national passport page with photo and date of birth, OR (b) university/school ID card with photo and date of birth. The most recent official document from your university/school proving your enrollment (not an admission letter). The most recent official transcripts and/or grade reports from your university/school. Visa page in your passport OR residence permit. Passport data page with a clear photo. You will be asked to upload these documents while completing the online application form.
selection: Two letters of recommendation are required: One of the two letters must come from a faculty member at your current university. The second recommendation can come from any non-family member (for example, a mentor or supervisor) who can attest to your character and/or work. At least one of the two recommenders must have known you for at least one year. Please contact two people from whom you wish to request a letter of recommendation. After receiving their confirmation, you will need to enter their email addresses in the application form. Each of your references will receive an email with a link from the Embark application system to submit their recommendation. You will be notified by Embark once their recommendations have been submitted.
countryNote: Be a national of a country listed on MMEG's list of eligible countries. Please refer to the MMEG Eligible Countries List on our website.
domainNote: There are no restrictions regarding fields of study. The scholarship is open to all women, or those who identify as women, who intend, after completing their degree, to work in or with a developing country to improve the lives of women and/or children.
levelNote: Be enrolled (not just admitted or accepted) in a certified university or school in France at the time of application; plan to be enrolled for a full academic semester after receiving the MMEG scholarship; and plan to graduate no later than three years after being awarded the MMEG scholarship.

synthese: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Sciences Po aims to support talented African students through their studies and to offer the next generation of leaders a world-class social science education, so they can go on to become changemakers in their home countries.
description: Since 2017, Sciences Po in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation, supports African students with an outstanding academic record and strong leadership potential, who face financial barriers, to give them access to a world-class social sciences education. Graduates of the Program are driven by a desire to make a real and lasting impact on the foremost issues facing the African continent.
